topics.summary: DescriptionHow to protect the firewall itself with the Intrusion Prevention System (IPS).ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSometimes, it may be necessary to protect a FortiGate unit itself from any vulnerabilities which could affect it.As of FortiOS 7.2.6/7.4.1 and above, it is now possible to use the Virtual Patching feature.Requirements to use the feature:FortiGuard reachability.Active IPS and FMWR licenses.Every local-in policy necessary to enable and use virtual patching is enabled under each VDOM with interface access.VDOM context:config firewall local-in-policy edit 0 set intf "any" set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set action accept set service "ALL" set schedule "always" set virtual-patch enable endFor example, take the vulnerability FG-IR-26-188.FortiGates can be protected with Virtual Patching if the FMWP DB is updated to 26.113 or any newer DB version, and if the necessary local-in policy is configured.To verify this, execute the following command in a global context:diagnose autoupdate versions | grep -i fmwp -A 5 -B 1 FMWP Definitions --------- Version: 26.00117 signed Contract Expiry Date: Thu Nov 12 2026 Last Updated using manual update on Wed Nov 11 11:05:11 2026 Last Update Attempt: Wed Nov 11 11:05:11 2026If the database is not updated, perform the Troubleshooting steps explained in "execute update-now" command fails to execute.

topics.title: EVPN Multihoming and MCLAG Deployment Considerations on FortiSwitch
topics.summary: DescriptionA scenario where unexpected MAC address loops, MAC flapping, and improper MAC route advertisements occur when EVPN Multihoming and an MCLAG setup are configured simultaneously across leaf switches. ScopeFortiSwitch Spine (3032E) and Leaf switches (1048E, 2048F).Feature: EVPN Multihoming / VXLAN. SolutionSymptomsObserving unexpected MAC address loops, MAC flapping, or improper MAC route advertisements (endpoints connected to a single leaf being advertised or learned across multiple leaf interfaces unexpectedly).Configuration incorporates both an MCLAG setup between two leaf switches and an EVPN Multihoming design simultaneously.CauseAn architectural conflict arises when attempting to combine MCLAG between two leaf switches with EVPN Multihoming in the same topology. FortiSwitch architecture does not support MCLAG between two separate leaf switches in an EVPN multihoming design framework.If MCLAG is deployed between two leaf switches, local port aggregation handles redundancy natively at the layer-2 boundary, rendering EVPN dual-homing/multihoming redundancy mechanisms redundant and conflicting. This mismatch can result in control-plane loops, incorrect MAC synchronization, and unexpected forwarding behavior. SolutionTo resolve and prevent loops in your network design, choose one of the following architectural approaches depending on your redundancy requirements:Pure EVPN Multihoming ESI-based design: Remove the MCLAG-ICL interconnect between the leaf switches. Treat each leaf switch as an independent node running Ethernet Segment Identifier configuration for multihomed servers/hosts, allowing BGP EVPN to manage redundancy and split-horizon filtering natively.Traditional MCLAG design: If using an MCLAG pair for server-facing redundancy, rely entirely on the local MCLAG domain without adding an overarching EVPN dual-homing layer across those specific switches.

topics.title: FortiGate enters Conserve Mode due to WAD memory leak associated with FortiGuard agent
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes an issue where FortiGate enters Conserve Mode due to excessive memory consumption by the WAD process, associated with the FortiGuard agent module 'wad_m_ftgd_agent'.The issue occurs when the WAD process experiences abnormal memory allocation, eventually causing the FortiGate to enter Conserve Mode.ScopeFortiGate, FortiOS 7.6SolutionThe FortiGate may experience excessive memory consumption by the WAD process, eventually entering Conserve Mode.The following symptoms may be observed.Gradually increasing memory consumption by the WAD process.FortiGate periodically entering Conserve Mode.Abnormally high memory allocation associated with 'wad_m_ftgd_agent'.Memory consumption remains high even when traffic levels are relatively stable.Temporary recovery after restarting the affected WAD process.Verify the memory utilizationRun the following commands to check the current memory usage and Conserve Mode status:get system performance status diagnose hardware sysinfo memory diagnose sys print-conserve-infoReview the memory utilization and confirm whether the FortiGate has entered Conserve Mode. The following crash log messages may be observed:service=kernel conserve=on msg="Kernel enters memory conserve mode" service=kernel conserve=exit msg="Kernel exits memory conserve mode"Identify the process consuming excessive memoryRun the following commands:diagnose sys top-mem 20 diagnose sys top-all 1 100 3In the affected environment, one WAD process was consuming approximately 3.15 GB of memory, representing around 40% of the system memory. Example output:wad (15780): 3309824kB node (284): 97783kB ipsengine (17650): 78861kBThe corresponding process utilization showed:wad 15780 R 99.5 41.1 7These results indicate unusually high memory consumption by a WAD process.Identify the WAD module responsible for memory allocationRun the following command to collect detailed memory information for the WAD processes:diagnose wad memory reportReview the output for excessive memory allocation associated with 'wad_m_ftgd_agent'.In the affected environment, the module showed the following memory allocation:id allocs frees reallocs avg_sz in_str active bytes max 75 395925 0 0 2176 36425008 395925 861728698 861728698 object name: wad_m_ftgd_agentThe module had approximately 395,925 active allocations, with no corresponding memory releases.The memory allocation associated with 'wad_m_ftgd_agent' reached approximately 822 MB.To inspect the specific WAD memory allocation category, run:diagnose wad memory track 75Example output:wad_id allocs frees reallocs avg_sz in_str active bytes max pid process 2500 403377 0 0 2176 37110592 403377 877947976 877947976 15780 user-info-0The output shows that memory allocations continue increasing without corresponding releases.Note: The memory allocation category ID may vary between firmware versions. Identify the appropriate category from the WAD memory report before executing the tracking command.Workaround and resolutionThe recommended solution is to upgrade to a supported FortiOS release containing the correction.The fix was integrated into the following engineering builds.FortiOS 7.6.8 build 3767. This is a special build that can be requested with TAC support.FortiOS 8.0.1As a temporary recovery measure, restarting the affected WAD process may release the accumulated memory. However, this does not resolve the underlying issue, and the memory consumption may increase again.Restarting WAD processes can interrupt active sessions and proxy-based traffic inspection. Perform this action during an appropriate maintenance window.For further information about restarting WAD processes, refer to the related article below.Related articles:Technical Tip: How to restart the WAD processTroubleshooting Tip: Conserve mode due to the IPS engine or WADTechnical Tip: Collect report for WAD high memory related issue for Fortinet TAC assistanceVerify the WAD process while firewall on conserve modeTechnical Tip: Overview of WAD process structure

topics.title: Technical Tip: Retrieve configuration file using GUI or CLI from a FortiManager
topics.summary: Description This article describes how the configuration file of a FortiGate can be retrieved by a FortiManager through the GUI or the CLI. Retrieving the configuration file using CLI can be used to gather more debug information if the retrieval process fails in the GUI. Scope FortiManager. Solution Via GUI: From: Device Manager -> Device & Group, as shown below: Select the managed FortiGate for which it is necessary to retrieve the configuration. Scroll down until the section: Configuration and Installation is visible; Click the button to the right of the Total Revision number called: Revision history. In the section that appears on the right, there is the Retrieve config button. Via CLI: Use the following debug to retrieve the OID of the device in question: diagnose dvm device list Once the OID value is known, the following command can be executed to retrieve the configuration file of the device in question: diagnose test deploymanager reloadconf <----- OID value from the previous step. Sample Configuration: diagnose dvm device list --- There are currently 2 devices/vdoms managed --- TYPE OID SN HA IP NAME ADOM IPS FIRMWARE fmg/faz enabled 158 FGVM0X00000XXXX - 10.5.60.3 FGVM010000****** root 6.00741 (regular) 5.0 MR4 (7605) |- STATUS: db: not modified; conf: out of sync; cond: unknown; dm: autoupdated; conn: down |- vdom:[3]root flags:1 adom:root pkg:[imported]FGVM010000****** Where the OID will be 158 for the respective FortiGate: diagnose test deploymanager reloadconf 158 Note: This operation is possible if the FGFM tunnel between the FortiGate and the FortiManager is up; otherwise, it will be necessary to perform troubleshooting as explained in Troubleshooting Tip: How to troubleshoot connectivity issues The following is an explanation of when it is useful to perform the Retrieve: FortiManager device settings and sync status Related articles: Technical Tip: How to fix synchronization issue in FortiManager Technical Tip: How to do bulk retrieve config in FortiManager using a script

topics.title: Web traffic interrupted for wireless users after upgrading 2GB/4GB FortiGate device
topics.summary: DescriptionWireless clients connected using tunnel-mode SSID may fail to access websites after upgrade when hardware acceleration is enabled.ScopeFortiOS 7.6.5 and higher. NP6XLite platforms such as FortiGate-60F.SolutionEndpoints connecting to Tunnel mode wireless SSIDs may experience web browsing issues owing to lost return packets. Protocols that tend to use smaller packet sizes such as ICMP and SSH continue to function normally. Endpoints with wired network connectivity, or endpoints connecting to Bridge mode are not affected.The issue has been reported on FortiGate and FortiWiFi platforms using SOC4 and NP6XLite architecture running FortiOS 7.6.5 and higher.WorkaroundImplement any of the options below to reduce TCP packet size or disable hardware offloading.Firewall Policy adjustments:Disable hardware offloading on the affected firewall policy: (Technical Tip: FortiGate Disable Hardware Acceleration).config firewall policy edit set auto-asic-offload disable next endConfigure a lower TCP Maximum Segment Size (MSS) on the firewall policy handling the wireless client traffic: (Technical Tip: Setting TCP MSS value).config firewall policy edit set tcp-mss-sender 1200 set tcp-mss-receiver 1200 next endChange the firewall policy mode from flow to proxy: (Technical Tip: Changing the inspection mode of the firewall).config firewall policy edit set inspection-mode proxy next endWireless Controller adjustments:Disable CAPWAP offload:config system npu set capwap-offload disable endAfter disabling capwap-offload, restart the wireless controller with execute wireless-controller restart-acd to apply the change. Note this will temporarily disrupt all wireless traffic.To avoid traffic disruption from the above process, see Technical Tip: How to disable CAPWAP offloading for FortiAPs without disrupting wireless traffic.Configure the FortiAP to apply tcp-mss-adjust to all TCP traffic as shown in Technical Note: IP fragmentation over wireless controlled based connections.config wireless-controller wtp-profile edit set ip-fragment-preventing tcp-mss-adjust set tun-mtu-uplink 1200 set tun-mtu-downlink 1200 next endInstead of FortiAP Profile settings, you can override the settings for a specific FortiAP as shown in IP fragmentation of packets in CAPWAP tunnels.config wireless-controller wtp edit FAPxxxxxxxx set override-ip-fragment enable set ip-fragment-preventing tcp-mss-adjust set tun-mtu-uplink 1200 set tun-mtu-downlink 1200 next endSymptoms:The issue is under investigation. One of the observed symptoms is a wireless traffic session offloaded successfully in the forward but not the reverse direction.To confirm traffic offload status, capture the session information for a failing HTTPS connection while hardware offloading is enabled.diagnose sys session filter src diagnose sys session filter dport 443 diagnose sys session listAn affected session should show the ips_offload and ofld-O flags, but no ofld-R flag. This indicates the forward direction is processed through the IPS/nTurbo fast path, while the reply direction is not successfully offloaded to NP6XLite.For example:npu_state=0x003494 ips_offload ofld-O

topics.title: Behavior of "set group-name" in FortiGate for SSL VPN portals
topics.summary: DescriptionThe behavior of "set group-name" when FortiGate is assigning a SSL VPN portal.ScopeFortiGate 7.2, 7.4.SolutionWhen external authentication is perfomed for SSL VPN Portals, the attribute "set group-name" can influence which SSL VPN Portal is assigned to a user.The two scenarios shown below have a user defined in Radius Server and assigned to TEST-GROUP:FGT-LAB # diagnose test authserver radius FAC-RADIUS pap testuser PASSWORD authenticate 'testuser' against 'pap' succeeded, server=primary assigned_rad_session_id=12232116637697 session_timeout=0 secs idle_timeout=0 secs! Group membership(s) - TEST-GROUPThe VPN portals assigned to each group:config vpn ssl settings set banned-cipher SHA1 SHA256 SHA384 set servercert "Fortinet_Factory" set source-interface "port3" set source-address "all" set default-portal "web-access" config authentication-rule edit 1 set groups "LOCAL_TEST" set portal "Portal-A" next edit 2 set groups "RADIUS_RESTRICTED" set portal "Portal-B" next end endGroup-Names are assigned to both User Groups:FGT-LAB # show user group config user group edit "SSO_Guest_Users" next edit "Guest-group" set member "guest" next edit "LOCAL_TEST" set member "FAC-RADIUS" config match edit 1 set server-name "FAC-RADIUS" set group-name "LOCAL-ONLY" next end next edit "RADIUS_RESTRICTED" set member "FAC-RADIUS" config match edit 1 set server-name "FAC-RADIUS" set group-name "TEST-GROUP" next end next endThe user now logs in and it lands on the correct VPN Portal, i.e., Portal B:Also confirmed by "fnbamd" debug logs:[591] __group_match-Group 'RADIUS_RESTRICTED' passed group matching [594] __group_match-Add matched group 'RADIUS_RESTRICTED'(3) [206] find_matched_usr_grps-Passed group matchingLOCAL_TEST Group is unassigned its group name "LOCAL-ONLY":FGT-LAB # show user group config user group edit "SSO_Guest_Users" next edit "Guest-group" set member "guest" next edit "LOCAL_TEST" set member "FAC-RADIUS" next edit "RADIUS_RESTRICTED" set member "FAC-RADIUS" config match edit 1 set server-name "FAC-RADIUS" set group-name "TEST-GROUP" next end next endNote that LOCAL-ONLY is missing.The user lands in Portal A despite "testuser" being assigned to "TEST_GROUP". This is because FortiGate does not have a defined "group-name" to match against the group attribute received from the RADIUS server.fnbamd debug:[631] fnbam_user_auth_group_match-req id: 11149760102407, server: FAC-RADIUS, local auth: 0, dn match: 0 [585] __group_match-Check if FAC-RADIUS is a group member [591] __group_match-Group 'LOCAL_TEST' passed group matching [594] __group_match-Add matched group 'LOCAL_TEST'(2)

topics.title: How to fix error "ssid is used by vap in same vdom" after upgrading version 7.6.8
topics.summary: DescriptionA commit failure occurs during the FortiManager installation validation stage when an existing wireless Virtual Access Point (VAP) is perceived as a duplicate, preventing the deployment of new SSID configurations.ScopeFortiManagerSolutionDuring the Install Wizard validation stage in FortiManager, the process fails while copying objects. The Install Preview cannot be opened because the validation ends with "Copy Failed". The FortiManager log displays the following error:Copy device global objects Copy objects for vdom root Commit failed: error -999 - ssid is used by vap, , in same vdomIf the same duplicate SSID needs to be used in different VAPs, the configuration should be as shown below: Technical Tip: How to use a duplicate SSID (same SSID name, different backend configuration).This particular scenario explains the issue when there is no intetntion to use the same SSID in different VAPs.Checking where the SSID is used with the "Where used" option does not provide extra information about why the conflict occurs.It is possible to unset the failing SSID to the default "fortinet" SSID by running the CLI script against the ADOM and Policy DB:config wireless-controller vap edit " " unset ssid endAfter doing this, the Installation Preview will not throw the same error message and may indicate which VAP the same SSID will be installed on. If it is not the correct configuration, it is possible to run the same script against "VAP #2" and later configure SSID correctly for each VAP respectively in the GUI.

topics.title: Troubleshooting certificate errors in FortiToken Mobile version 6.7.1 and above
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiToken Mobile version 6.7.1 and above may show a certificate error when it connects to an on-premises FortiAuthenticator or FortiGate during push approval, token activation, or token export (moving tokens to a new phone). The app cannot verify the server certificate because it is untrusted, expired, or not valid for the address the app used to connect.Tokens issued through the Fortinet cloud service are not affected because cloud endpoints use publicly trusted certificates. A certificate error can still occur if a TLS-inspecting proxy intercepts the connection, or if the trusted root certificates on the device are outdated.ScopeFortiToken Mobile version 6.7.1 and above on Android, connecting to an on-premises FortiAuthenticator or FortiGate.SolutionIdentify the error.FortiToken Mobile displays the Untrusted Certificate screen. Depending on the error, the app blocks the connection or offers Allow once, Always allow, and Block (cancel).For example:The server's certificate is not from a trusted certificate authority. The app offers Allow once, Always allow, and Block.Select Allow Once or Always Allow only if thinking that the certificate is valid, or after the administrator confirms that it is valid and correct.The certificate issue must still be resolved on the server.Verify the server certificate.The system administrator must verify the server certificate against the following requirements, and correct or replace it where it does not comply.Subject Alternative Name (SAN).FortiToken Mobile matches the connection address against the SAN entries only. The Common Name (CN) is not used for this validation.A certificate with the correct hostname in the CN but no matching SAN entry is rejected, except in the case described under SAN verification exception. The SAN must contain the exact hostname or IP address used by the app.SAN verification exception.FortiToken Mobile version 6.7.1 and above on Android skips the hostname check against the SAN when the payload fingerprint already proves the identity of the server. Certificate expiry is still enforced.Certificate validity.Confirm that the certificate is within its validity period.notBefore is the date from which the certificate becomes valid.notAfter is the date on which the certificate expires.Renew or replace the certificate if it has expired or is not yet valid.Signature algorithm.The certificate must use a signature algorithm of SHA-256 or stronger. Certificates signed with SHA-1 or MD5 are rejected. Reissue the certificate using SHA-256 or a stronger supported algorithm.Self-signed certificate trust.A self-signed certificate is rejected unless explicitly chosen to trust it. FortiToken Mobile offers Allow once and Always allow when it encounters a self-signed certificate.Trusting a self-signed certificate does not resolve an address mismatch. The certificate must still contain the correct hostname or IP address in its SAN. Otherwise, the retry fails with a hostname mismatch error.Certificate verification checklist.The hostname or IP address configured in FortiToken Mobile matches one of the entries in the certificate SAN, unless the SAN verification exception applies.The notBefore and notAfter dates cover the current date.The signature algorithm is SHA-256 or stronger.Any self-signed certificate is explicitly trusted, where applicable.Retest.After correcting the certificate:Restart the service on FortiAuthenticator or FortiGate.Retry push approval on the mobile device.Retry adding a token, where applicable.Confirm that the certificate error no longer appears.Reinstalling FortiToken Mobile or reactivating tokens is not required after the server certificate has been corrected.Expected outcome.When the server presents a valid certificate that matches the address used by FortiToken Mobile, is within its validity period, and meets the required signature algorithm standard, the affected connections succeed. If the error persists, recheck the SAN entries, the certificate validity dates, the signature algorithm, and the exact address used by the app.

topics.title: Analytics retention status remains one day below the configured limit and does not reach 100% in FortiAnalyzer 7.6.6.
topics.summary: DescriptionOn FortiAnalyzer 7.6.6, the analytics retention status shows 89 out of 90 configured days (98%) and never reaches the full 90 days (100%).Scope FortiAnalyzer.SolutionThis is a known issue in FortiAnalyzer 7.6.6 where the analytics retention does not correctly reach the configured limit.Solution:Upgrade FortiAnalyzer. Upgrade the device to one of the following versions where this issue is resolved:FortiAnalyzer 7.6.7, build 3685 and laterFortiAnalyzer 8.0.0, build 0054 and laterWorkaround: If an upgrade is not immediately possible, increase the configured retention period by one day. For example, if 90 days of retention are required, set the "Keep logs for Analytics" setting to 91 days. The system trimming process will remove the boundary day, effectively leaving the required 90 days of data. Apply this same logic to any other ADOM configured with a different retention period by adding one day to the current setting.

topics.title: Unable to modify Pre-Login Disclaimer when VDOM is enabled
topics.summary: DescriptionThe pre-login disclaimer is not displayed as configured when accessing the FortiGate GUI, even though the pre-login disclaimer has been configured.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionThe FortiGate is configured with separate MGMT and Traffic VDOMs. Users access the GUI through a web browser using the Management IP address assigned to an interface in the MGMT VDOM. The pre_admin-disclaimer-text message is configured under the following path in the Global VDOM. config system replacemsg admin "pre_admin-disclaimer-text" set buffer "PRE WARNING: This is a private computer system. Unauthorized access or use is prohibited and subject to prosecution and/or disciplinary action. Any use of this system constitutes consent to monitoring at all times and users are not entitled to any expectation of privacy. If monitoring reveals possible evidence of violation of criminal statutes, this evidence and any other related information, including identification information about the user, may be provided to law enforcement officials. If monitoring reveals violations of security regulations or unauthorized use, employees who violate security regulations or make unauthorized use of this system are subject to appropriate disciplinary action. end However, when users access the GUI, a different disclaimer message is displayed instead of the configured pre_admin-disclaimer-text. To troubleshoot this issue, verify the following settings in the MGMT VDOM when users access the GUI through an IP address assigned to an interface in that VDOM. Access the MGMT VDOM.Run the following command to verify whether pre_admin-disclaimer-text is configured. config vdom edit config system replacemsg-group edit "default" set comment "Default replacement message group." config admin edit "pre_admin-disclaimer-text" set buffer "Warning ** Disclaimer" set header none set format none next end next end Workaround:Delete the replacemsg-group configured in the MGMT VDOM.config vdom edit config system replacemsg-group delete default next end

topics.title: Adding VXLAN to an existing VLAN
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to configure VXLAN without removing existing references to the VLAN or physical interfaces.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionThe article VXLAN over IPsec for multiple VLANs using software switch gives steps to configure a VXLAN between two remote sites.One requirement of that configuration is that the VLAN interfaces must have no references and no IP addresses before you can add them to a software switch or a virtual wire pair.This can be challenging in setups where the VLAN interface has numerous references, because the firewall administrator may be concerned about the impact of modifying them.It is possible to avoid reconfiguring the existing VLAN interface using the steps below. This requires creating a second VDOM, as well as access to an external LAN switch. Refer to Technical Tip: How to enable multiple VDOMs for more information on how to enable multi-vdom mode.Warnings:Adding and deleting additional VDOMs is a maintenance activity and can affect network access in rare scenarios. It is strongly recommended to only add or delete VDOMs during a maintenance window.The second/new VDOM is required to isolate sessions passing over the VXLAN from sessions on the main VDOM VLAN. If the external switch workaround is used without a second VDOM, the VXLAN will have high internal packet loss.Option 1: New VDOM without direct connection to the internet (Virtual IP and NPU link).Create the new VDOM (You can also use a pre-existing VDOM that does not contain the existing VLAN interface).Global VDOM: Assign an unused physical port on the firewall to the new VDOM. Assign IP addresses and VDOMs to each side of the VDOM link. See Inter-VDOM routing.config system interface edit "internal1" set vdom next edit "npu0_vlink0" set vdom set ip 10.10.150.1 255.255.255.252 next edit "npu0_vlink1" set vdom set ip 10.10.150.2 255.255.255.252 next endMain VDOM: Configure a virtual IP and firewall policy on the main VDOM to allow IPsec traffic, with an external IP that is not used for other IPsec traffic and an internal IP matching the remote (New VDOM) side of the VDOM link.config firewall vip edit "VIP_ipsec" set service "ESP" "IKE" set extip 198.51.100.102 set mappedip "10.10.150.2" set extintf "wan1" next end config firewall policy edit set name "ipsec vip inbound" set srcintf "wan1" set dstintf "npu0_vlink0" set action accept set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "VIP_ipsec" set schedule "always" set service "IKE" "ESP" next endMain VDOM: Configure an IP pool and firewall policy to allow outbound IPsec traffic from the New VDOM.config firewall ippool edit "ippool-198.51.100.102" set startip 198.51.100.102 set endip 198.51.100.102 set arp-reply disable next end config firewall policy edit set name "ipsec vip outbound" set srcintf "npu0_vlink0" set dstintf "wan1" set action accept set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set schedule "always" set service "IKE" "ESP" set nat enable set ippool enable set poolname "ippool-198.51.100.102" next endNew VDOM: Configure an IPsec tunnel using the inter-VDOM link as the parent interface. Configure a firewall policy to enable the IPsec tunnel and a route to the tunnel's remote gateway over the inter-VDOM link.config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit "S2S_VPN" set interface "npu0_vlink1" set ike-version 2 set peertype any set net-device disable set proposal aes256-sha256 set psksecret set nattraversal forced set dhgrp 20 set remote-gw 192.0.2.101 next end config vpn ipsec phase2-interface edit "S2S_VPN" set phase1name "S2S_VPN" set proposal aes256-sha256 set dhgrp 20 next end config firewall policy edit set name "VPN_policy" set srcintf "VPN" set dstintf "VPN" set action accept set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set schedule "always" set service "ALL" next end config router static edit set dst 192.0.2.101 255.255.255.255 set gateway 10.10.150.1 set device "npu0_vlink1" next endNew VDOM: Configure VXLAN over IPsec tunnel as shown in Technical Tip: VXLAN over IPsec with virtual wire pair,New VDOM: Configure a virtual wire pair containing the New VDOM's physical port and the VXLAN interface facing the FortiGate New VDOM interface as an access port in the existing VLAN to be bridged. For example:config system virtual-wire-pair edit "vwp" set member "internal1" "vxlan10" next endConfigure the external switch's physical port connected to new VDOM's physical port with the access VLAN matching the VLAN already in use. If the external switch is a managed FortiSwitch, this is done in the VDOM containing the FortiLink interface.config switch-controller managed-switch edit "Managed_Switch" config ports edit "port1" set vlan "DATA-VLAN10" next end next end Option 2: New VDOM has a direct connection to the internet.Similar to Option 1, but without the need for an inter-VDOM link or Virtual IP. Instead, assign an interface with a public IP address to the new VDOM and terminate the IPsec VPN on that interface.Once the VPN is configured in the new VDOM, complete the configuration as described in this article:Technica

topics.title: Upgrading non-production FortiGate devices without following a supported Upgrade Path
topics.summary: Description A procedure to upgrade an inventory or non-production firewall to a current FortiOS version for redeployment or testing without the need to follow a supported upgrade path. Scope Physical FortiGate platforms. Solution This procedure demonstrates how to install a target FortiOS firmware image directly on a spare FortiGate running an older FortiOS version, without performing intermediate firmware upgrades in a supported upgrade path. After the installation, a factory reset must be performed to discard the previous configuration and initialize the device with the factory-default configuration of the newly installed firmware. Prerequisites Spare FortiGate: The device must not be in production, and the existing configuration must not be required, as it will be erased during the procedure.GUI access: You must have access to the FortiOS GUI. Usually, this requires a laptop connected to a physical interface of the FortiGate, with HTTPS administrative access enabled.Serial console access: You must have access to the FortiOS serial console. Usually, this requires a console cable connected between the FortiGate and the same laptop. Verify that console access is working as expected before starting the procedure, and maintain it throughout the process. It provides recovery options and an additional management channel.Physical access to the device: Physical access is required to power cycle the device if needed for recovery.Firmware availability: Verify that the target FortiOS firmware image is available for the specific FortiGate model.Firmware License (if the current firmware is FortiOS 7.4.2 or higher): Starting with FortiOS 7.4.2, the device must have an active firmware entitlement to upgrade to a later FortiOS branch. The device must have internet access, at least temporarily, to verify its firmware entitlement. If no firmware license is available, refer to Installing firmware from system reboot for the available upgrade method. Procedure Download the target firmware image by following Downloading a firmware image.Upgrade the FortiGate from the FortiOS GUI by manually uploading the firmware image, following Upgrading individual devices. Review and confirm any upgrade warnings.Note: The firmware management page may have a different name depending on the FortiOS version. Depending on the FortiOS branch, it may be accessible from one of the following locations:System -> FirmwareSystem -> Fabric ManagementSystem -> Firmware & RegistrationAfter the unit reboots, verify the upgrade status using a console connection.Verify the installed FortiOS version using get system status | grep -if '^version'.Example output:FortiGate-201E # get system status | grep -if '^version' Version: FortiGate-201E v8.0.2,build0251,260928 (GA.F) <--- FortiGate-201E #Note 1: Since you are not following a supported upgrade path, the device may fail to boot. If this occurs, this upgrade method is not applicable. Refer to Technical Tip: Boot the backup firmware and config via console to recover the previous firmware and configuration, then use one of the following alternative upgrade methods:Upgrade from the BIOS using a TFTP server. See Installing firmware from system reboot.Upgrade by following an approved upgrade path. See Technical Tip: Manual firmware upgrade by referring to an upgrade path. Note that a firmware license is likely required when using this method, even if the current firmware version is FortiOS 7.2 or lower, because one of the intermediate versions will implement the upgrade restriction described in Prevent firmware upgrade depending on the current firmware license's expiration date.Note 2: If the device upgrades successfully, configuration error messages are still likely because the upgrade did not follow a supported upgrade path. Since the device will be factory reset in the next step, these errors can be disregarded unless they affect administrative access. If needed, execute diagnose debug config-error-log read to review the configuration errors.Perform a factory reset.Access the FortiGate CLI using either the built-in CLI Console in the GUI or an external console connection.Enter the following command to initiate a factory reset:execute factoryresetWhen the confirmation prompt appears, enter y to proceed:This operation will reset the system to factory default! Do you want to continue? (y/n)Wait for the FortiGate to complete the factory reset and reboot.The device has now been returned to factory-default settings, running the new firmware version. Configure the device by following the FortiGate QuickStart Guide for the relevant device platform, and verify GUI access.

topics.title: FortiAP clients unable to obtain IP address via DHCP
topics.summary: DescriptionWireless clients cannot receive an IP address from the DHCP server despite the server sending DHCP Offer packets. This is caused by insufficient Power over Ethernet (PoE) amperage provided to the FortiAP.ScopeFortiAP, FortiGate, FortiSwitch.SolutionSymptoms: Wireless clients can see the SSID and enter the correct password, but they fail to obtain an IP address via DHCP. Packet captures show that the DHCP server responds to the DHCP Discovery with a DHCP Offer, but the client never sends a DHCP Request.Root cause: The FortiAP is connected to a PoE source that provides insufficient amperage. In this case, the PoE source provided 55V - 0.6A, while the FortiAP requires 55V - 1.09A to operate correctly. This power deficiency prevents the FortiAP from processing the DHCP handshake properly.Resolution:Verify the power requirements of the FortiAP model in use.Check the PoE output specifications of the switch or PoE injector providing power to the FortiAP.Ensure the PoE source meets or exceeds the required voltage and amperage (e.g., 55V - 1.09A).Connect the FortiAP to a PoE switch or injector that provides the required power specifications.Verify that wireless clients can now successfully obtain an IP address via DHCP.Troubleshooting steps to identify the issue:If clients cannot obtain an IP address, perform the following captures to determine where the DHCP process fails:Run a sniffer on the FortiAP CLI to monitor DHCP traffic:diag_sniffer any "port 67 or port 68" 6 0 lRun the following debug commands on the FortiGate to monitor the DHCP server process:diagnose debug application dhcps 255 diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug enableAfter reproducing the failure, stop the debug commands with:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug resetCompare the Transaction IDs between the FortiGate and FortiAP. If the FortiGate sends a DHCP Offer but the FortiAP does not forward a DHCP Request from the client, verify the physical power supply to the FortiAP.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Migrate SAML authentication from SSL VPN to dial-up IPsec IKEv2 while keeping SSL VPN in service
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to add SAML authentication to a dial-up IPsec IKEv2 remote-access VPN on a FortiGate that already runs SSL VPN with SAML, without modifying or interrupting the existing SSL VPN service.ScopeFortiOS v7.2, v7.4, v7.6.SolutionA frequent question during SSL VPN to IPsec migrations is whether the existing SAML configuration, both the FortiGate SAML object and the Identity Provider (IdP) application, can simply be reused for IPsec. The answer is that the IdP tenant, users, groups, and claim design are reused, but the Service Provider (SP) endpoints are not: SSL VPN and IPsec are two distinct SPs on the same FortiGate, reachable on different TCP ports, and each requires its own SAML object and its own IdP application registration.This article covers the design considerations, port planning, FortiGate and IdP configuration, FortiClient deployment, a phased migration plan, verification commands and the failure points most often seen in support cases.Design considerations:SAML for IPsec requires IKEv2. SAML authentication for dial-up IPsec is supported only with IKEv2. IKEv1 is not supported. FortiClient v7.4.4 and above no longer support IPsec IKEv1 at all.SAML is not carried inside IPsec. The SAML exchange happens over a separate TCP session before the tunnel is established:The user selects connect in FortiClient.FortiClient opens a TCP session to the FortiGate on the port defined by auth-ike-saml-port.The FortiGate returns a redirect containing the SAML Authentication Request and the IdP URLs.FortiClient opens the embedded or system browser, the user authenticates at the IdP, and the SAML Response with the assertions is returned to FortiClient.FortiClient posts the SAML Response to the FortiGate. The FortiGate validates the assertion against the IdP certificate and issues a temporary token ID.FortiClient starts IKEv2 negotiation and presents the token ID during EAP. The tunnel comes up.The practical consequence is that the FortiGate must be reachable on the SAML TCP port from the client network in addition to UDP/500, UDP/4500 or the IKE TCP port.A native OS IKEv2 client cannot be used. Browser-based SAML for dial-up IPsec is a FortiClient/FortiGate implementation. The Windows built-in IKEv2 client and other third-party clients cannot complete this flow.Port planning: This is the step that most often breaks an otherwise correct configuration when SSL VPN must stay in service.Service Port used:For the existing SSL VPN, keep it unchanged, typically TCP/443. Do not modify during the migration;For IPsec IKEv2, UDP transport UDP/500 and UDP/4500. No conflict with SSL VPN;IPsec over TCP, if required, ike-tcp-port, such as TCP/8443 or TCP/10443, must not collide with the SSL VPN port;IPsec SAML listener auth-ike-saml-port, default TCP/1001, must not collide with SSL VPN, admin access, or ike-tcp-port;Notes:The default value of auth-ike-saml-port is 1001. Any free TCP port is acceptable; 9443 and 10443 are common choices when 1001 is filtered on client networks.In FortiOS v7.6.1 and later, the SAML service also listens on ike-tcp-port. Fortinet recommends keeping ike-tcp-port and auth-ike-saml-port on different ports so that the authd daemon does not process IKE TCP packets. Using a single shared port is possible but is a deliberate design choice, not the default.Changing auth-ike-saml-port flushes existing IPsec tunnels, so it is recommended to apply it in a maintenance window.Where a spare public IP or a dedicated FQDN is available, use it for the IPsec service. Full IP separation removes the port planning problem entirely and makes rollback trivial.To determine whether the existing Entra ID Enterprise Application should be reused:Create a second Enterprise Application dedicated to IPsec.A second Enterprise Application for IPsec is recommended so the SSL VPN application is never touched. This provides an independent rollback, it separate sign-in logs per service, and Conditional Access can be scoped per VPN technology.Add IPsec URLs to the existing SSL VPN application. Some IdPs allow multiple Reply URLs, but the Identifier (Entity ID) is normally single-valued, and any edit or certificate rotation on that application affects live SSL VPN users. Not recommended in production.Copy the following from the SSL VPN application to the new one: user and group assignments, NameID format, username claim, group claim configuration, Conditional Access and MFA policies, and signing options.Change only the SP-specific values:Identifier (Entity ID): https:// : /remote/saml/metadata.Reply URL (ACS): https:// : /remote/saml/login.Logout URL: https:// : /remote/saml/logout.Where is the name that FortiClient will contact and is the value configured in auth-ike-saml-port.FortiGate configuration: configure the SAML listener port.config system global set auth-ike-saml-port 9443 endConfigure the certificate presented to FortiClient.FortiClient validates the certificate that the FortiGate presents on the

topics.title: Configure SNMP monitoring for FortiClient EMS
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiClient EMS supports SNMP polling and traps for remote monitoring. Use SNMP polling to query system metrics such as CPU usage, network bandwidth, and disk usage.ScopeFortiClient EMS 7.4.5, build 2111.SolutionRun the commands below at the interactive EMS CLI prompt. On a virtual appliance, connect to EMS over SSH. On a non-appliance installation, start the CLI from the Linux terminal with sudo emscli.Configure SNMP monitoringEnable performance monitoringEnable performance monitoring on the installed EMS server.config set perfmon --enableIn the FortiClient EMS console, go to Dashboard -> Performance to confirm that the dashboard is available. See EMS Performance dashboard in 7.4.5.Configure SNMP and the trap destinationconfig set snmp --enabled true --snmp.host : --snmp.community " "Replace the placeholders with the trap receiver's IP address and listening port, and the SNMP community string.FortiClient EMS sends traps to the destination configured in --snmp.host. For polling, configure the SNMP manager to query the EMS server's IP address on UDP port 161.EMS SNMP configuration command.Verify the settings and test pollingconfig get snmp enabled config get snmp snmp.host config get snmp snmp.communityConfirm that SNMP is enabled and that the trap destination and community string match the intended settings. EMS SNMP verification command.Load FORTINET-FORTICLIENTEMS-build 2111.M.mib into the SNMP manager or MIB browser.From the manager, run an SNMP GET against a known EMS object identifier (OID) or an SNMP WALK against an EMS subtree. Confirm that EMS returns values. Use the MIB that matches the installed EMS build. See FortiClient EMS 7.4.5 MIB file.Troubleshoot SNMP polling timeoutsConfirm that the manager targets the correct EMS IP address and that the firewall allows polling traffic to UDP port 161 on EMS and permits the replies.Check that the community string configured on the manager matches the EMS setting.Identify the EMS interface and IP address used for polling.system get infoStart a capture on that interface, then repeat the GET or WALK from the SNMP manager.execute pcap --if --filter "udp port 161" --out snmp-polling.pcapNo request reaches EMS. Check the destination IP, routing, and firewall rules between the manager and EMS.A request reaches EMS, but no response leaves. Check the return path and firewall rules between EMS and the manager.Capture SNMP polling traffic on FortiClient EMS.

topics.title: False positive anti-replay (replayed packet) drops on NP7 platforms when npu-offload is enabled on phase1-interface
topics.summary: DescriptionAnti-replay (replayed packet) drops are seen on NP7 platforms at or around rekeys when npu-offload is enabled on phase1-interface.ScopeFortiOS, NP7 platforms.SolutionOn NP7-based FortiGates such as FortiGate-401F, inbound ESP packets consisting of three or more fragments can cause anti-replay errors, even though the packets are neither duplicated or replayed.WorkaroundImplement one of the following configurations to prevent the unintended drops from anti-replayDisable npu-offload on phase1-interface of the affected tunnel.config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit set npu-offload disable next end Disable anti-replay on the phase2-interface of the affected tunnel. This disables all anti-replay drops.config vpn ipsec phase2-interface edit set replay disable next end Enable NP7 ip-reassembly (this is not recommended in most environments that would be affected by this issue, since it causes additional latency in environments with many packets consisting of three or more fragments.)config system npu config ip-reassembly set status enable end endResolutionAn enhancement is scheduled for FortiOS 8.0.3 to enable configuring the espff-proc option under config system npu. This setting affects how the NP7 counts fragmented ESP packets when ip-reassembly is disabled.config system npu set espff-proc endWhen to disable espff-proc:Continuous inbound ESP traffic fragmented into more than two fragments.Consistent anti-replay (replayed packet) drops observed, especially during or immediately after a rekey.Disabling npu-offload on the phase1-interface no longer shows anti-replay (replayed packet) drops.

topics.title: FlowSphera: a free NetFlow analyzer I built on a FortiWiFi-40F
topics.summary: Hi all,I wanted to see monthly traffic on my FortiWiFi-40F at home, and that grew into a full NetFlow analyzer. Since people here ask about third-party collectors from time to time, I would like to share it and hear what is missing for FortiGate users. What it shows: - Traffic by host, service, country and interface, with conversations and new conversations - Path analysis: how traffic moves through your network - Application names, if Application Control is on the firewall policies (a monitor-only profile is enough) - Security events, PDF reports by e-mail, AD/LDAP sign-in and an API The free Community edition has every feature and two limits: 5,000 flows/s and 30 days of history. A license only raises those limits. This is the configuration on my 40F (FortiOS 7.4.13): config system netflow set active-flow-timeout 60 config collectors edit 1 set collector-ip set source-ip next end end config system interface edit "wan" set netflow-sampler both next endAdd the sampler to your internal interfaces too if you want traffic between your own networks. Two limits to keep in mind: Wi-Fi SSID interfaces cannot be sampled, so traffic between two SSIDs stays invisible, and FortiOS exports only sessions created after the sampler was enabled.It installs on a Linux server with one line: https://github.com/telesphera/flowsphera

topics.title: Technical Tip: Using log aggregation to migrate logs
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to use Log Aggregation to Migrate Logs to another (possibly new) FortiAnalyzer, providing an example and some tips for troubleshooting.This is the recommended approach for migrating logs when both old and new FortiAnalyzer units are simultaneously active. Log aggregation is also useful when using local Collectors to forward logs to a central Analyzer.ScopeFortiAnalyzer. CLI syntax valid for FortiAnalyzer 6.4 and later.SolutionAggregation is only available if the old FortiAnalyzer is still reachable and operational.Note: Some low-end FortiAnalyzer models may not be able to act as aggregation servers.Client side (on the old FortiAnalyzer):config system log-forward edit 1 set mode aggregation set agg-user set agg-password set agg-time set server-addr set server-name next endUse 'set server-ip' to set new FortiAnalyzer IP address.Use 'set server-name' to add a descriptive string.Server-side (on the new FortiAnalyzer):config system admin user edit "aggradmin" set password password set profileid "Super_User" set adom "all_adoms" end config system log-forward-service set accept-aggregation enable endDebug commands:execute tac report diagnose debug application log-aggregate 8 diagnose debug enable execute log-aggregation all. diagnose sniffer packet any ”port 3000” 3 0 a Use 'execute log-aggregation all' to specify one aggregation-client entry, or all.

topics.title: FortiClient VPN-only 7.4.3 – IPsec disconnect breaks Windows L2TP/IPsec (errors 789/791) – Still unresolved
topics.summary: Our municipality and affiliated public institutions have invested in Fortinet equipment and solutions for over a decade. It is extremely disappointing that a mature product branch has been left with a serious, reproducible regression affecting essential public services.Technical details: OS: Windows 11 Pro 25H2 and 26H2 Product: FortiClient VPN-only (IPsec) Affected builds: 7.4.3.4726 and 7.4.3.6002 (probably all versions from ~7.4.1?) Steps: Connect FortiClient IPsec → disconnect → attempt Windows native L2TP/IPsec VPN. Result: Windows VPN fails with RAS errors 789/791. Confirmed workaround: Restarting the Windows IKEEXT service immediately restores connectivity. Network routing and adapter states appear normal after disconnect. This issue has been publicly reported since at least February 17, 2025, with no confirmed permanent fix. Even the latest security-maintenance build, 7.4.3.6002, still reproduces it.Related reports: Feb 17, 2025: https://community.fortinet.com/support-forum-92/issues-connecting-to-l2tp-ipsec-after-connect-use-forticlient-with-another-vpn-198838 Sep 4, 2025: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5544865/l2tp-connection-attempt-failed-because-security-po Oct 2, 2025: https://community.fortinet.com/support-forum-92/unclean-disconnect-with-ipsec-vpn-215459 Nov 27, 2025: https://community.fortinet.com/support-forum-92/issues-connecting-to-l2tp-ipsec-after-connect-use-forticlient-with-another-vpn-219026 Restarting privileged system services is not an acceptable solution in security-conscious public institutions where users operate without administrator rights.Discontinuing free VPN-only development while leaving such regressions unresolved creates the unfortunate impression that customers are being pressured into paid migration. Whether intentional or not, this is unacceptable for organizations managing extensive legacy infrastructures under strict security requirements and limited public budgets.Migration cannot always happen immediately. Security updates should not come at the expense of essential functionality.We ask Fortinet to finally investigate and fix this issue, provide an official workaround suitable for non-administrator users, or release a corrected VPN-only build. Please provide a bug ID and a clear resolution plan.

topics.title: LLDP management IP address advertisement requirements
topics.summary: DescriptionThe conditions required for FortiGate to advertise a management IP address in the LLDP Management Address TLV.LLDP advertisements may be transmitted successfully while the Management Address TLV is not included.The management IP address is advertised only when specific LLDP, interface, management access, and High Availability (FGCP) requirements are met.ScopeFortiGateLLDPFGCP High AvailabilitySolutionFortiGate includes a Management Address TLV in LLDP advertisements only when all of the following conditions are satisfied.LLDP transmission must be enabled.LLDP transmission must be enabled through one of the following configuration contexts. If LLDP transmission is disabled, FortiGate does not advertise a management address.config system global set lldp-transmission enable endconfig system settings set lldp-transmission enable endUsing port25 as an example:config system interface edit "port25" set lldp-transmission enable next endThe LLDP egress interface must have an IPv4 or IPv6 address.The interface transmitting LLDP packets must have either an IPv4 address or an IPv6 address configured. If the interface does not have an IPv4 or IPv6 address, the Management Address TLV is not included in LLDP advertisements.Example:config system interface edit "port25" set ip 10.47.0.108 255.255.255.0 next endThe LLDP egress interface must have a management protocol enabled in "allowaccess".The interface must permit at least one of the management protocols e.g. HTTP, HTTPS, SSH, Telnet, or SNMP.Example:config system interface edit "port25" set allowaccess https ssh next endHow FGCP High Availability affects the setup:When FGCP High Availability is not enabled, the management address TLV is advertised if all previous requirements are satisfied.When FGCP High Availability is enabled, the LLDP egress interface must belong to a VDOM that is hosted on the HA "primary unit" to advertise the management address TLV.If the LLDP egress interface belongs to a VDOM that is hosted on the HA "secondary unit", FortiGate does not include the management address TLV in LLDP advertisements.If the HA reserved management interface feature is enabled, and since the assigned management interface configuration is not part of the HA synchronization, the LLDP advertisements will include the management address TLV in both primary and secondary units' management interface.Example for LLDP advertisement not including the management address TLV:Example for LLDP advertisement including the management address TLV:

topics.title: A workaround if pre-configured virtual appliance template is not availble in cloud environment
topics.summary: DescriptionA workaround to use when a pre-configured virtual appliance template is not available on the respective platform soon after a new firmware image is released.ScopeFortiGate in Cloud platforms.SolutionPre-configured virtual appliance templates such as AMI (Amazon Machine Image) and Azure VM Image are being used to spin up FortiGate (or Fortinet products) in cloud environments quite quickly and easily, as the required OS is built with it.However, there are cases where these pre-configured virtual appliance templates are not updated right after firmware images are released to the public, or where some of the variants are not available in the cloud environment.The following is an example from AWS where an AMI is not available for ARM64 BYOL:7.6.8 (build3744) - 2026-10-20 — 3 of 4 (no ARM64 BYOL)ARM64 BYOL: not publishedARM64 On-Demand: ami-0xxxxxxxxxxxxxx86 BYOL: ami-0xxxxxxxxxxxxxx86 On-Demand: ami-0xxxxxxxxxxxxxxAs a solution or a workaround, it is possible to spin off the VM using an earlier version pre-configured virtual appliance template, then download the respective firmware image from FortiCloud, upload it to the VM, and then upgrade the device.Important notes & best practicesAlways match architecture (x86_64 vs ARM64). Cross-architecture upgrades are not supported.Follow the recommended upgrade path. Jumping major versions can cause issues.Take configuration backups and OS disk snapshots before upgrading, especially in production.For PAYG / On-Demand instances, ensure you use the correct image variant; otherwise you may see “firmware image didn’t pass signature verification” or FortiGuard license errors.In HA or Autoscale environments, plan the upgrade carefully (suspend health checks / scaling processes if needed) and update the launch configuration / scale-set image afterward.Marketplace images are eventually published; once available, prefer deploying new instances directly from the official image for cleanliness and supportability.Licensing: After upgrade, verify that the VM license is still valid and that FortiGuard services are connected.

topics.title: FortiDeceptor quarantine integration not working in non-management VDOMs in FortiGate
topics.summary: DescriptionSteps to repair FortiDeceptor IP ban functionality with multiple VDOMs on a FortiGate operating in a multi-VDOM environment. Note that FortiDeceptor automatic quarantine actions apply only to the root or management VDOM on FortiGate devices, so they do not block traffic in other VDOMs.ScopeFortiGate, FortiDeceptor.SolutionWhen integrating FortiDeceptor with FortiGate for automatic quarantine, the IP ban action only appears in the root or management VDOM. The quarantine does not propagate to other VDOMs or devices in the Security Fabric, and traffic in those VDOMs is not blocked.The FortiDeceptor integration uses a REST API to send Fabric events to FortiGate. This REST API is a management-plane feature and does not pass through non-management VDOMs. Consequently, the IP ban action is only executed within the root or management VDOM.To extend IP Ban enforcement, either route non-management VDOM traffic to the management VDOM or grant the connector access to non-management VDOMs.Route the affected traffic through an "npu.vlink" to the root VDOM so the IP ban applied there can effectively block the traffic.To grant the fabric connector in the root VDOM access to the specific non-management VDOMs, run the following commands in the CLI:config system csf edit fabric-connector set vdom end endIf no VDOMs are specified, the connector has access only to the VDOM through which it joined the Security Fabric.After this change, re-test the integration (trigger a decoy interaction from FortiDeceptor and verify the ban appears in the target VDOM(s)).Add automation actions for the integration manually. For detailed steps on configuring the webhook for quarantine integration, review the following article:FortiDeceptor quarantine integration with FortiGate over Webhook.

topics.title: NP7 QTM shaping statistics are not reset by diagnose netlink interface clear
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article explains a case where diagnosing the netlink interface clear appears to clear those statistics, but the next read after traffic resumes from the pre-clear accumulated value instead of counting up from zero.ScopeFortiGate 7.6.3 or later.SolutionWhen it happensThis occurs on FortiGate models with NP7 processors, FortiOS 7.6.3 and later, where a traffic shaping profile is applied to the interface with set npu-offloading enable (the default), so that offloaded traffic is shaped by QTM. Which statistics are affectedThe three per-class counters inside the egress traffic control: block, and only for classes that carry shaped, NPU-offloaded traffic:forwarded_bytesdropped_packetsdropped_bytes SymptomApply an egress shaping profile with set npu-offloading enable to an interface and send traffic through a shaped class.Run the following command to read the class counters:diagnose netlink interface list Run the following command to clear the counters:diagnose netlink interface clear Immediately run the following command again to re-read the same counters:diagnose netlink interface list -> forwarded_bytes, dropped_packets and dropped_bytes for that class show 0.Send traffic again and re-read: the values reappear carrying the pre-clear accumulation rather than starting from zero. A second clear behaves the same way. Fix and WorkaroundThere is no clear workaround for this issue. As currently planned, it will be fixed in FortiOS 7.6.9 and 8.0.3 or later. Until a fixed build is in use, take two readings of the counter and calculate the rate from the difference between them. Related Document:diagnose netlink interfaceQTM traffic shaping exampleTechnical Tip: Important changes to traffic shaping on FortiGate with NP7 queuing-based traffic management (QTM) module

Everything was working fine before...Setup: FortiGate 200F HA – FortiOS 7.2.14 EMS Cloud 7.4.8 (build 2245) FortiClient Windows 7.4.8 All ZTNA connections fail with No end-point info found, but the actual issue seems to be somewhere between FCNACD and WAD.EMS is connected and verified, WebSocket is up, and the FortiGate receives endpoint UIDs, certificates and ZTNA tags.We've already collected FCNACD and WAD debug logs. Here's what we're seeing:FCNACD:ZTNA record: Exists: true, Complete: falseZTNA record is incompleteMandatory field "mac" absentError updating primary macWAD:DevQueryResp code=NoEntrydev resp is nok:1dev resp tid=0, rsp=(nil)dev tag matching, info=(nil), tag_cnt=0POLICY DENIEDWAD queries by UID and IP also return Response termination due to no more data.Interestingly, the EMS API (/api/v1/report/fct/sysinfo) returns incomplete endpoint data, missing fields like user_name, fct_ver and fct_build_no, even though EMS itself displays them correctly.We've already tried re-verifying EMS, reconnecting it, adding a second connector, restarting the relevant processes, checking policies, etc... No luck :/Has anyone seen something similar? Especially WAD returning NoEntry even though FCNACD has the endpoint UID, certificate and tags?Also, does anyone know exactly which fields FCNACD expects from /api/v1/report/fct/sysinfo for a ZTNA endpoint record to be considered complete (Complete: true)? Could missing fields such as MAC, username or FortiClient version cause this, even when the endpoint has the correct compliance tag? Any ideas or workarounds would be appreciated…

topics.title: Technical Tip: Migrate config to a different model FortiGate using FortiManager
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to migrate the config from a FortiGate model to a different model using FortiManager. Scope FortiManager. Solution Migrating config involves 2 parts: device settings (including all the templates) and policy package. Migration of Device Settings. In this article, copy over device-level settings by capturing the configuration in provisioning templates (this applies to System Settings, SDWAN, Static Routes, BGP, and IPSec Tunnels): Device Manager -> Provisioning Templates -> Select the template type -> More -> Import. Note: Another approach to migrate device settings is to use FortiConverter, as discussed in Technical Tip: How to replace FortiGate with a different model in FortiManager. This step will import all IPsec tunnels from the old device and save their configurations as a template. Then select the old device from the drop-down list: Any required changes, such as 'Outgoing Interface', can be applied before assigning the template to the new FortiGate. Same steps apply for other types of templates (i.e., BGP template, SD-WAN template, etc). Notes: Interfaces (VLANs, zones, ...) will not be imported by these templates; the interfaces must be manually created either in Device Manager GUI or via a script that runs against the Device Manager. Check any templates assigned to the old FortiGate that may be needed for the new and assign those. Policy & Objects. The Policy Package of the old FortiGate can be assigned to the new FortiGate by modifying the 'Installation Targets' in the Policy Package. Interfaces used in the Policies are the 'Normalized Interfaces' that need to be mapped to the physical interfaces. Below is an example of a Normalized interface 'Data', it needs to be mapped to the device interface on the new FortiGate via per-device mapping or per-platform mapping. Once all the templates and policy package are ready, perform the install in steps. Install only device settings first, so all the interfaces are created. Install Policy Package after confirming the normalized interface mappings are correct.

topics.title: Technical Tip: How to enable STUN protocol in policy
topics.summary: Description This article describes how to enable the STUN protocol in a firewall policy. Scope FortiOS in the default NGFW profile-based mode (with or without Central SNAT enabled). Solution STUN is a protocol used to allow UDP communication through a NAT device, such as an external firewall. Most commonly, it is used as a supporting protocol for VoIP technologies such as SIP; for more information, see the article Technical Tip: How STUN resolves SIP NAT issue. By default, STUN configuration options are hidden in policies. Attempting to enable them generates an error. FW01 # config firewall policy FW01 (policy) # edit 99 FW01 (99) # set permit-stun-host enable command parse error before 'permit-stun-host' Command fail. Return code -61. FW01 (99) # To enable configuring STUN options, ensure the firewall policy handling outgoing VoIP signaling traffic has NAT enabled. config firewall policy edit set action accept set nat enable set permit-any-host disable set permit-stun-host disable next end STUN options on firewall policies leverage expectation sessions to match incoming traffic from remote endpoints. Expectation sessions are more commonly encountered when working with FortiOS session helpers; see the article Technical Tip: Session helpers and expectation sessions. Difference between 'permit-stun-host' and 'permit-any-host': The two available STUN options cannot both be enabled on the same policy, since they define different NAT methods. When 'set permit-any-host enable' is configured on the firewall policy or an associated IP pool, when outgoing UDP traffic is sent, the firewall will create an expectation session to match incoming UDP packets from any IP address and port, provided the destination IP address and port match the original external Source IP address and port. This is also known as 'full cone NAT', see this document: Full cone NAT for fixed port range IP pools. While this is the most flexible NAT method for STUN, it has a higher potential to allow unwanted UDP traffic to pass through to the original host. When 'set permit-stun-host enable' is configured on a firewall policy or an associated IP pool, the expectation session includes the original destination IP address the client sent UDP traffic to. Incoming traffic will only match the expectation session if sourced from this IP address. This is also known as 'Address Dependent NAT' or 'Restricted Cone NAT'. Related documents: RFC 3489 RFC 5389

topics.title: After upgrade to FortiOS 7.4.13, user receives error "400 Bad Request" when using proxy inspection and Deep Packet inspection
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading to FortiOS 7.4.13, a user may start receiving "Error 400: Bad Request" when accessing legitimate sites when the firewall policy is set to use Deep Packet Inspection and proxy-based inspection.ScopeFortiOS 7.4.13.SolutionFollowing an upgrade to FortiOS 7.4.13, users may start seeing the Error 400 Bad Request when accessing legitimates sites: This issue is present when the following settings are in place:strict-web-check is set to enable:config web-proxy global set strict-web-check enable endFirewall policy using proxy-mode inspection and a Deep Packet inspection profile:config firewall policy edit 40 set name "Outbound Internet" ... set inspection-mode proxy set ssl-ssh-profile "custom-deep-inspection" ... next end FortiOS 7.4.13 introduced a change that enables strict-web-check: FortiOS 7.4.13 Release notes | Changes in default behavior.The reason the traffic is blocked is because enabling strict-web-check under config web-proxy global caused the proxy mode policy to block HTTP/2 requests that carry more than one Cookie header field. HTTP/2 (per RFC 7540 8.1.2.5) permits the Cookie header to be split into multiple separate header fields, but strict mode rejected such requests as malformed, returning a connection error to the client.Enhancements to allow split-cookies while strict-web-check is enabled will be implemented in future FortiOS release 7.4.15.SolutionIf legitimate web traffic is blocked after upgrade, the previous behavior can be restored with the following configuration option:config web-proxy global set strict-web-check disable end

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Troubleshooting the error 'Failed to download log disk status from FIM, please reset FPMx'
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes an issue observed on the FortiGate 7k chassis platform where some FPMs fail to rejoin the chassis following an unexpected power outage.ScopeFortiGate 7000F series.SolutionThe issue mentioned in this article was observed on several FPMs within the chassis following a power outage. After power was restored, the management and data heartbeat interfaces of the affected modules transitioned to a failed state, accompanied by the error message shown below: 'Failed to download log disk status from FIM, please reset FPMx'.Run the command below to determine the slots that are getting this error:TestFW [FIM01] (global) # diagnose load-balance status Slot: 2 Module SN: FIM11FTB00000001 Primary FPM Blade: slot-3 Slot 3: FPM10FTB00000013 Status:Working Function:Active Link: Base: Up Fabric: Up Heartbeat: Management: Good Data: Good Status Message:"Running" Slot 4: FPM10FTB00000014 Status:Working Function:Active Link: Base: Up Fabric: Up Heartbeat: Management: Good Data: Good Status Message:"Running" Slot 5: FPM10FTB00000015 Status:Working Function:Active Link: Base: Up Fabric: Up Heartbeat: Management: Good Data: Good Status Message:"Running" Slot 6: Status:Dead Function:Active Link: Base: Up Fabric: Down Heartbeat: Management: Failed Data: Failed Status Message:"Failed to download log disk status from FIM, please reset FPM6." Slot 7: Status:Dead Function:Active Link: Base: Up Fabric: Down Heartbeat: Management: Failed Data: Failed Status Message:"Failed to download log disk status from FIM, please reset FPM7." Slot 8: Status:Dead Function:Active Link: Base: Up Fabric: Down Heartbeat: Management: Failed Data: Failed Status Message:"Failed to download log disk status from FIM, please reset FPM8."In this scenario, power cycling or FRU reset is not fixing the issue by itself. The recommended workaround is to run the commands shared below for each slot to restart the base backplane connection and power cycle the slot. fnsysctl ifconfig b-slot down fnsysctl ifconfig b-slot up

topics.title: Troubleshooting the error "Failed to download log disk status from FIM, please reset FPMx"
topics.summary: DescriptionAn issue observed on the FortiGate 7k chassis platform where some FPMs fail to rejoin the chassis following an unexpected power outage.ScopeFortiGate 7000F series.SolutionThe issue mentioned in this article was observed on several FPMs within the chassis following a power outage. After power was restored, the management and data heartbeat interfaces of the affected modules transitioned to a failed state, accompanied by the error message shown below: "Failed to download log disk status from FIM, please reset FPMx".The FIM (FortiGate Interface Module) holds the log disks (typically two 4 TB SSDs in RAID-1 on FIM-7921F/FIM-7941F). FPMs need to retrieve log-disk status from the FIM during startup/rejoin. A transient base-backplane or communication glitch after power loss can prevent this, leaving the FPM in a failed state even though basic power and Base link may be up.Run the command below to determine the slots that are getting this error:TestFW [FIM01] (global) # diagnose load-balance status Slot: 2 Module SN: FIM11FTB00000001 Primary FPM Blade: slot-3 Slot 3: FPM10FTB00000013 Status:Working Function:Active Link: Base: Up Fabric: Up Heartbeat: Management: Good Data: Good Status Message:"Running" Slot 4: FPM10FTB00000014 Status:Working Function:Active Link: Base: Up Fabric: Up Heartbeat: Management: Good Data: Good Status Message:"Running" Slot 5: FPM10FTB00000015 Status:Working Function:Active Link: Base: Up Fabric: Up Heartbeat: Management: Good Data: Good Status Message:"Running" Slot 6: Status:Dead Function:Active Link: Base: Up Fabric: Down Heartbeat: Management: Failed Data: Failed Status Message:"Failed to download log disk status from FIM, please reset FPM6." Slot 7: Status:Dead Function:Active Link: Base: Up Fabric: Down Heartbeat: Management: Failed Data: Failed Status Message:"Failed to download log disk status from FIM, please reset FPM7." Slot 8: Status:Dead Function:Active Link: Base: Up Fabric: Down Heartbeat: Management: Failed Data: Failed Status Message:"Failed to download log disk status from FIM, please reset FPM8."Note the affected slots (6, 7, 8 in this example).In this scenario, power cycling or FRU reset is not fixing the issue by itself. The recommended workaround is to run the commands shared below for each slot to restart the base backplane connection and power cycle the slot. fnsysctl ifconfig b-slot down fnsysctl ifconfig b-slot upAfter the commands:Wait a few minutes for the FPM(s) to boot and rejoin.Re-check with diagnose load-balance status. Heartbeats and Fabric should become Good/Up and Status Message should change to "Running".Verify configuration sync: diagnose sys confsync status | grep in_sy

topics.title: HTTP 400 Bad Request error
topics.summary: DescriptionUsers encounter an HTTP 400 Bad Request error when launching secrets in FortiPAM version 7.0.0 after a passkey is registered and an Active Directory password change occurs.ScopeFortiPAM version 7.0.00.SolutionAfter upgrading FortiPAM to firmware version 7.0.0, users cannot launch secrets. The browser returns an HTTP 400 Bad Request error.This issue occurs even for users who do not have a registered passkey and authenticate with a standard username and password. Both native Remote Desktop and Web RDP launches are affected.Trigger condition:The issue is triggered when at least one user has a FIDO2 passkey registered in FortiPAM and a password change occurs for an Active Directory user. This combination causes the FortiPAM internal WAD process to reject launching requests by incorrectly identifying them as SSO launching requests that fail validation.WAD debug logs show the following error sequence:wad_pam_parse_parameters: Target only SSO launching username=xxx, 115:0 wad_pam_parse_parameters: Unexpected PAM launching request ..., err_code=5 wad_pam_token_alloc: fail to get security launcher!__wad_http_build_replmsg_resp: Generating replacement message. http request parse fail repmsg_id 0 Forward response from Internal: HTTP/1.1 400 Bad RequestThis is a known issue and currently under investigation.Workaround:To restore secret launching functionality:Remove all registered passkeys from all FortiPAM users.Instruct all users to log out of FortiPAM.Instruct all users to log back in to FortiPAM.After completing these steps, normal secret launching through the GUI is restored.

topics.title: FortiSwitch SCP Not Working After Upgrade – Error 501: Permission Denied
topics.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading the FortiSwitch, SCP file transfers stopped working and returned the following error:501 - Permission DeniedScopeFortiSwitch 7.6.7 and later releases.SolutionConfiguration and FindingsThe following TACACS+ remote authentication configuration was observed on the FortiSwitch:edit "name" set remote-auth enable set trusthost1 x.x.x.x x.x.x.x set trusthost2 x.x.x.x x.x.x.x set accprofile "no_access" set wildcard enable set remote-group "group" set accprofile-override enable nextThe following observations were made during troubleshooting:The accprofile-override setting is enabled.During authentication, the TACACS+ server returns the super_admin access profile.Direct SSH access using the same TACACS+ account works successfully, and the expected administrative privileges are available.SolutionStarting from FortiSwitch 7.6.7, SCP is no longer supported.To back up the switch configuration, use one of the supported file transfer protocols: SFTP, FTP, or TFTP.Unlike the previous SCP-based approach, starting from FortiSwitch 7.6.7, configuration backups must be initiated directly from the FortiSwitch. In this process, the FortiSwitch establishes an outbound connection to the SFTP, FTP, or TFTP server to transfer the configuration backup.Note: Use SFTP, FTP, or TFTP as alternatives to SCP when backing up FortiSwitch configurations on version 7.6.7 and later.

topics.title: Primary FortiGate GUI unavailable with "SSL_ERROR_BAD_MAC_READ" error after upgrading to 7.4.13
topics.summary: DescriptionThe web management GUI of the primary FortiGate unit becomes inaccessible with a TLS MAC error when virtual patching is enabled on a local-in policy.ScopeFortiGate, FortiManager.SolutionSymptomsAfter upgrading a FortiGate High Availability cluster to FortiGate version 7.4.13, the HTTPS management GUI of the primary unit is unavailable. Users attempting to connect via browser receive the following error message:Secure Connection Failed The page you are trying to view cannot be shown because the authenticity of the received data could not be verified. Error Code: SSL_ERROR_BAD_MAC_READThe following conditions are observed:SSH access to the primary unit remains functional.The management GUI of the secondary unit remains accessible.The issue is reproducible by enabling virtual patching on the local-in policy covering management HTTPS traffic. Root causeA regression in FortiOS 7.4.13 causes a TLS record MAC failure during the handshake when virtual-patch is enabled on a local-in policy that processes management HTTPS traffic on the primary unit of a High-Availability cluster. ResolutionThe fix for this issue is scheduled for release in FortiOS 8.0.3.Use one of the following workarounds to restore GUI access. Workaround 1: Disable virtual patchingDisable the virtual-patch setting on the local-in policy that matches management HTTPS traffic.Connect to the FortiGate via SSH.Run the following commands:config firewall local-in-policy edit set virtual-patch disable next end Workaround 2: Use a non-self-signed certificateChange the administrative server certificate from a self-signed certificate to a CA-signed certificate.Connect to the FortiGate via SSH.Run the following commands:config system global set admin-server-cert Fortinet_GUI_Server end

topics.title: Technical Tip: Explanation of IPsec VPN DPD Options and On-Idle tunnel flushing process
topics.summary: Description This article describes the operation process for IPsec VPN DPD options. Scope FortiGate, all firmware. Solution DPD options can be found in the GUI section: DPD modes on FortiGate: On-Demand. On-Idle. Disable. DPD mode can be configured in CLI with the following commands: config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit "VPN-NAME" ... set dpd 'Local FGT' -> Router -> 'Remote FGT' -> Remote Client. On-idle between both FortiGate devices, set to dpd-retrycount 3, dpd-retryinterval 10. Local Client -> Remote Client (ping). Remote FortiGateDevice external (line) interface DOWN. Below are the commands to take the ike debug on the firewall: diagnose vpn ike log-filter clear diagnose vpn ike log filter rem-addr4 x.x.x.x diagnose debug app ike -1 diagnose debug enable Stop the debug after the output is collected with the following commands: diagnose debug disable diagnose debug reset Note: If Dead Peer Detection values are modified on any IPsec peer during troubleshooting activities, the IPsec tunnel may renegotiate. Both peers maintain their own Dead Peer Detection timers and negotiation logic. Changing 'dpd-retrycount' or 'dpd-retryinterval' on one side may impact synchronization between peers and trigger a renegotiation of the tunnel. In production environments, changes to Dead Peer Detection settings should be performed with caution, as tunnel renegotiation may result in temporary service interruption. Before FortiOS v7.4.1, the command used to filter VPN IKE logs was 'diagnose vpn ike log-filter'. For further details, refer to Troubleshooting Tip: IPsec Tunnel (debugging IKE).
