topics.title: Using FortiAnalyzer to detect activities related to the Node2Shell Remote Code Execution | CVE-2026-111497
topics.summary: Description How to use a custom event/alert handler in FortiAnalyzer to raise alerts for incident response related to attacks that attempt to leverage the Node2Shell Remote Code Execution. A report is also provided to gain historical visibility into the logs. Note that this article provides alpha files which are automatically generated. The article will be continually updated as more information becomes available. Scope This article contains the files necessary to load a handler and report into the FortiAnalyzer for either a Fabric ADOM or a FortiGate ADOM. The Fabric report and handler leverage logs from other Fortinet products that can be used to detect the attack in addition to FortiGate logs. For more information about this attack, see the following FortiGuard Outbreak Alert: Node2Shell Remote Code Execution Solution What is included in Fortinet_Node2Shell Remote Code Execution.zip: Node2Shell Remote Code Execution.json: This event/alert handler helps identify Node2Shell Remote Code Execution detected by FortiGate and other Fortinet products. This event handler is configured for Fabric ADOMs. Node2Shell Remote Code Execution.dat: This report displays the findings on Node2Shell Remote Code Execution from FortiGate and other Fortinet products. It is configured for Fabric ADOMs. fgt_Node2Shell Remote Code Execution.json: The event/alert handler for FortiGate ADOMs is configured for FortiGate logs only. fgt_Node2Shell Remote Code Execution_report.dat: The report for FortiGate ADOMs includes FortiGate charts only. Steps: Download the Fortinet_Node2Shell Remote Code Execution.zip file (contains 4 files). Unzip Fortinet_Node2Shell Remote Code Execution.zip. Import Node2Shell Remote Code Execution_event-handler.json or fgt_Node2Shell Remote Code Execution_event-handler.json event handler: Choose an ADOM (if ADOMs are enabled). The ADOM may have the Fabric or FortiGate type. Open the Event Handlers pane (or Alert Handlers pane in FortiAnalyzer 8.0+). Select More -> Import. Select the appropriate handler from the unzipped folder depending on the ADOM type. Result: The handler is enabled and will be triggered if the appropriate logs are received following the import of the handler. Edit the handler to customize the notification section. Import Node2Shell Remote Code Execution_report.dat or fgt_Node2Shell Remote Code Execution_report.dat to Reports: Choose an ADOM (if ADOMs are enabled). The ADOM may have the Fabric or FortiGate type. Open the All Reports pane. Select More -> Import. Select the appropriate file from the unzipped folder for the ADOM type to add the report to the ADOM. Result: The Node2Shell Remote Code Execution_report can be run anytime as determined by an admin user.

topics.title: Mitigating CVE-2026-98432 using NPU fp-anomaly on FortiGate
topics.summary: Description A mitigation process for CVE-2026-98432, a critical (CVSS 3.1 9.8) use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel IPv4 TCP stack. FortiGate devices running on affected kernel versions can be protected at the NPU hardware level by dropping inbound TCP packets that carry IPv4 options. Scope FortiOS versions 7.4.x, 7.6.x, and 8.0.x. Solution This is an IPv4 packet diagram: The first byte of the IPv4 header contains two 4-bit fields: Version (4 bits) IHL - Internet Header Length (4 bits) Version can have only two values: 0100 - IPv4 0110 - IPv6 IHL can have different values. Minimum length is 20 bytes (no options) and maximum 60 bytes: 20 bytes (IHL 5) - 0101 (no options) 24 bytes (IHL 6) - 0110 28 bytes (IHL 7) - 0111 32 bytes (IHL - 1000 Wireshark capture without options: 0100 0101 = 45 (HEX): When the hexadecimal value is 45, it means IHL is 5 (20 bytes), with no options configured. Wireshark capture with options set: 0100 1000 = 48 (HEX): When the hexadecimal value is 46 or higher, it means IHL is > 5, with options configured.The attack requires the inbound TCP SYN packets to carry IPv4 options (IP Header Length > 20 bytes / IHL > 5).Dropping all inbound TCP packets that carry any IPv4 option at the NPU level is therefore an effective compensating control while a firmware update is not available. config system np6xlite edit np6xlite_0 config fp-anomaly set ipv4-optlsrr drop set ipv4-optssrr drop set ipv4-optrr drop set ipv4-opttimestamp drop set ipv4-optsecurity drop set ipv4-optstream drop set ipv4-unknopt drop endend Note: All IPv4 option types must be set to drop. The CVE can be triggered by any option that inflates the IP header length beyond 20 bytes. Covering only one option type leaves the device exposed to the remaining variants. For IPv4 options for which there isn't a specific command to set, they will be covered by ipv4-unknopt.After configuring the fp-anomaly under the NPU, drop counters can be checked with the command diagnose npu np6xlite anomaly-drop. FGT # diagnose npu np6xlite anomaly-dropIHP0:IHP1:ipv4_unknopt :0000000000000062022] ipv4_optrr :0000000000000050023] ipv4_opttimestamp :0000000000000050028]IHP2:IHP3:XHP0:XHP1:HTX0: IPS and virtual patching signatures were already released to protect hosts: Virtual Patching IPS Signature Related documents: PSIRT Advisory: FG-IR-26-188 Linux Kernel Remote Code Execution CVE-2026-98432 — NVD CVE-2026-98432 — cve.org FortiOS CLI Reference Guide

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Logs are not displayed in FortiGate log view when FortiAnalyzer is set as the source
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the issue where logs are not being displayed in the FortiGate log view when FortiAnalyzer is set as the source.ScopeFortiAnalyzer, FortiGate.SolutionWhen FortiAnalyzer is running in v7.4.11, it does not respond to FortiGate log queries. As a result, logs are not displayed in the FortiGate log view when FortiAnalyzer is set as the source (Whereas if the source is set to memory, logs are displayed).This issue may only affect the FortiGates that are part of the HA cluster. However, log receiving is not affected on the FortiAnalyzer side itself. They can still be viewed on FortiAnalyzer under LogView.FortiGate in standalone mode is not affected, and logs are displayed as usual (when source = FortiAnalyzer).To verify that the issue matches the issue reported in this article, execute the commands in FortiAnalyzer and then open a ticket with Fortinet TAC and upload the output:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug application fazsvcd 8 diagnose debug enableThis issue is fixed in FortiAnalyzer version 7.6.4 or above. Refer to the upgrade guide to check compatibility and the recommended release for FortiAnalyzer before planning upgrade activity (see the related articles section).For the v7.4 branch: The fix for this issue is scheduled in v7.4.12.Related articles:Customer Service Tip: How to create a ticket for Fortinet TACTechnical Tip: Recommended Release for FortiManager and FortiAnalyzerTechnical Tip: Upgrading FortiManager/FortiAnalyzerTroubleshooting Tip: Logs are not displayed in FortiView

FortiGate VXLAN traffic fails when LAN1 is a member of a software switch
topics.summary: DescriptionTraffic sourced from a FortiGate VLAN interface fails to communicate over a VXLAN tunnel when the LAN1 interface is part of the same software switch due to a MAC address conflict.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptoms.A user configures a VXLAN tunnel between two FortiGate devices. The VXLAN interface and the LAN1 interface are members of the same software switch. In this configuration, the following behavior occurs:Host-to-host traffic across the VXLAN tunnel works normally.Traffic sourced from the FortiGate VLAN interface fails to reach the remote site.Communication works if the LAN1 interface is removed from the software switch or if a different interface (such as LAN2) is used instead. Root cause.The issue is caused by a MAC address conflict. On certain FortiGate models, the Current_HWaddr (Virtual MAC) for the LAN1 interface is derived from the HA group-id. If two separate FortiGate clusters use the same group-id, they assign the identical Virtual MAC address to their respective LAN1 interfaces.When a VLAN interface is created on top of a software switch, it inherits the MAC address of the first member interface. If LAN1 is the first member, the VLAN interface uses the duplicated Virtual MAC. When the remote FortiGate receives a reply destined for this MAC, it matches its own local LAN1 entry and forwards the frame locally instead of encapsulating it back through the VXLAN tunnel, which results in the traffic being blackholed. Resolution.To resolve this conflict, change the HA group-id on one of the FortiGate clusters to ensure each device has a unique Virtual MAC address.Log in to the Command Line Interface (CLI) of one of the FortiGate devices.Run the following commands to change the group-id:config system ha set group-id endVerify that the MAC addresses on the LAN1 interfaces are now unique by running the following command on both devices:diagnose hardware deviceinfo nic lan1

topics.title: FortiClient does not apply the third DNS server pushed by the FortiGate when connecting to IPsec dial-up tunnel
topics.summary: DescriptionWhen a FortiGate dial-up IPsec tunnel is configured with three DNS servers, FortiClient 7.2.x installs only the first two on the Windows VPN adapter. The third (ipv4-dns-server3) is never applied, even though the FortiGate sends it correctly in the mode-cfg exchange. FortiClient 7.4 and later apply all three.ScopeFortiOS, FortiClient (Windows) 7.2.x, FortiClient(Windows) 7.4.3 and below.SolutionIn this scenario, FortiGate is configured with three DNS servers under phase1:config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit "Dialup" set ipv4-dns-server1 8.8.4.4 set ipv4-dns-server2 1.1.1.1 set ipv4-dns-server3 8.8.8.8 next end IKE debugs confirm all three DNS servers are sent via mode-cfg:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug application ike -1 diagnose debug enable ike V=root:0:Dialup_0:8265: mode-cfg send (3) IPv4 DNS(1) 8.8.4.4 ike V=root:0:Dialup_0:8265: mode-cfg send (3) IPv4 DNS(2) 1.1.1.1 ike V=root:0:Dialup_0:8265: mode-cfg send (3) IPv4 DNS(3) 8.8.8.8On the client side, only two DNS servers are shown under the VPN adapter:This is a FortiClient limitation in applying the mode-cfg DNS list to the Windows adapter, not a FortiGate configuration problem. The FortiGate supports up to three DNS servers for a dial-up tunnel as mentioned in Technical Tip: Setting multiple DNS server for IPsec dial-up VPN.Resolution:To resolve this limitation, upgrade to FortiClient version 7.4.7 or higher.Related articles:Troubleshooting Tip: DNS resolution over IPsec/SSL VPN

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer missing configuration after upgrade
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to troubleshoot missing configuration in FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer after an upgrade.ScopeFortiManager and FortiAnalyzer.SolutionBefore the upgrade:Using PUTTY SSH into FortiManager and run CLI commands:show execute tac reportAfter the upgrade:Using PUTTY SSH into FortiManager and run CLI commands:show execute tac reportCompare both before and after (show) files.Get back missing configuration:Copy the missing configuration from the (show) file.Paste it back into FortiManager via CLI console or PUTTY.Note: For (set password ENC ...) part need to replace as (set password CORRECT_PASSWORD) first, before paste it into FortiManager via CLI console or PUTTY.

topics.title: FortiManagement Cloud VPN reports for IPSec Dial-up ikev2 shows IP address instead of username
topics.summary: DescriptionVPN reports in FortiManagement Cloud display the user IP address in the User field instead of the actual username for Dial-up IPsec IKEv2 VPN connections.ScopeFortiGate, FortiManagement Cloud.SolutionSymptoms.After configuring Dial-up IPsec VPN, the VPN reports generated in FortiManagement Cloud show the IP address of the connecting client in the User field. The expected behavior is to see the authenticated username to identify the parties and their session usage.To ensure the system captures the necessary user information in the logs, follow these steps:Select VPN -> IPsec Tunnels and edit the VPN configuration.Change the authentication user group setting to 'Inherit from policy'.Select Policy & Objects -> Firewall Policy and specify the required user group on the firewall policies governing the VPN traffic.Note: While this ensures the username is present in the eapuser field of the VPN event logs, the FortiManagement Cloud reports may still display the IP address.Root cause.This is a limitation in current versions of FortiManagement Cloud. The reporting engine does not currently map the eapuser field from the event logs to the User field in the Top Dial-up VPN Users charts.Permanent fix.Fortinet is improving the VPN reporting functionality. The upcoming version 26.4.a of FortiManagement Cloud will update the Top Dial-up VPN Users chart and all related IPsec user charts to use the eapuser field for consistency. This update is tentatively scheduled for release in the first week of December 2026.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Automation stitch to reboot managed FortiAP from FortiGate
topics.summary: Description This article shows how to configure the automation stitch to reboot the managed FortiAP daily at a desired time. Scope FortiGate v7.2.x and v7.4.x. Solution Here are the commands to configure this automation stitch for 1 AM for example: config system automation-stitch edit "Restart_AP_stitch" set trigger "restart_ap_trigger" config actions edit 1 set action "Restart_AP_action" set required enable next end next end config system automation-trigger edit "restart_ap_trigger" set trigger-type scheduled set trigger-hour 1 ---> scheduled for 1 AM, this can be changed as desired. next end config system automation-action edit "Restart_AP_action" set action-type cli-script set script "execute wireless-controller reset-wtp all" set accprofile "super_admin" next end Note: To reboot a specific FortiAP, replace the script with 'execute wireless-controller reset-wtp '. To restart multiple FortiAP (and not all), the command is 'execute wireless-controller reset-wtp '. WTP-group is the FortiAP group. Related article: FortiAP groups

topics.title: "CMDB get request for sensitive information table" System Event logs when making changes on the dashboard
topics.summary: DescriptionThe meaning of the System Event log ID 44562, "CMDB get request for sensitive information table", and an explanation of why it appears after making changes on the Dashboard.ScopeFortiOS 7.6.SolutionIn this scenario, an administrator logged into the GUI and changed the CPU timeframe from 30 minutes to 1 hour under Dashboard -> Status.As a result, FortiOS logged "CMDB get request for sensitive information table" followed by an "Object attribute configured" log as shown below:Example raw logs:date=2026-11-04 time=07:40:41 eventtime=1793806840205720745 tz="-0800" logid="0100044562" type="event" subtype="system" level="warning" vd="root" logdesc="CMDB get request for sensitive information table" msg="A request is being made by process /bin/httpsd (pid 9242) to table system.admin" date=2026-11-04 time=07:40:43 eventtime=1793806842463090027 tz="-0800" logid="0100044547" type="event" subtype="system" level="information" vd="root" logdesc="Object attribute configured" user="admin" ui="https(10.9.x.x)" action="Edit" cfgtid=131072565 cfgpath="system.admin" cfgobj="admin" cfgattr="gui-dashboard:1[widget:7[timeframe[30-min->1-hour]]]" msg="Edit system.admin admin"This log message will appear when httpsd (the GUI/REST daemon) reads a sensitive CMDB table such as system.admin or system.accprofile. From the example above, because the config path is system.admin, the "CMDB get request for sensitive information table" message is logged.Starting from 8.0.0, the gui-dashboard sub-table is moved from system.admin and system.dashboard-collection, which means the "CMDB get request for sensitive information table" log message will no longer appear after making changes in the Dashboard.Related article:44562 - LOGID_EVENT_CONFIG_SENSITIVE_INFO

topics.title: FortiManager ADOM upgrade from 7.4 to 7.6 fails with remote certificate invalid error
topics.summary: DescriptionInstructions to fix ADOM upgrade failure due to a remote certificate invalid error.ScopeFortiManager.SolutionAn Administrative Domain (ADOM) upgrade from version 7.4 to 7.6 fails due to a remote certificate missing its PEM wrapper, resulting in a certificate invalid error.SymptomsWhen attempting to upgrade an ADOM from version 7.4 to 7.6 in FortiManager, the process fails with the following error message:Fail (errno=-2):This remote certificate is invalidRoot causeThe upgrade fails because one or more remote certificates in the ADOM database are stored without the required PEM wrapper (the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- and -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines). While the certificate may be valid for current operations, the ADOM upgrade process to version 7.6 rejects certificates that do not follow this standard format.ResolutionRestore the PEM wrapper to the affected certificate using a script.Step 1: Identify the problematic certificateSelect Policy & Objects -> Advanced -> Remote Certificate in the root ADOM.Review the entries for certificates that appear incomplete, expired, or use default names.Use the Where Used feature to check if the suspicious certificate is referenced in SAML or PKI user configurations.Run the ADOM Upgrade Readiness check for the root ADOM and export the report to identify the specific affected object.Step 2: Fix the certificate wrapperTake a FortiManager configuration backup.Select Device Manager -> Scripts in the root ADOM and create and import the script with wrapper details that restores the PEM wrapper.config vpn certificate remote edit "certificate" set remote "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- Do not change the certificate content -----END CERTIFICATE-----" set range global next endRun the script against any policy package in the root ADOM. Because certificates are shared ADOM objects, the change applies to the entire ADOM.See How to add a script.Step 3: Complete the ADOM upgradeSelect System Settings -> ADOMs. Select the ADOM and upgrade it to version 7.6.Before installing changes to the FortiGate devices, run an install preview on devices using the modified certificate (such as those using SAML) to confirm there are no unexpected configuration changes.Troubleshooting the upgrade failureIf the ADOM upgrade continues to fail, capture debug logs by running the following commands in a session with logging enabled:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug enable diagnose debug timestamp enable diagnose debug service cdb 255 diagnose debug service dvmdb 255 diagnose debug service dvmcmd 255 diagnose debug service sys 255 diagnose debug service main 255Retry the upgrade until it fails, then stop the debug process with:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug disable

topics.title: Understanding IPsec DH-group compatibility and default changes in FortiOS 7.6.5
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiOS 7.6.5 introduces changes to the default Diffie-Hellman (DH) groups used in IPsec Phase 1 and Phase 2 configurations. These changes can affect IPsec tunnel negotiation when the remote VPN peer does not support the updated DH groups.This article explains the default DH-group changes, their impact on existing configurations, and how to verify DH-group compatibility between VPN peers.ScopeFortiGate devices running FortiOS 7.6.5 and later.SolutionUnderstand the default DH-group changes.Starting with FortiOS 7.6.5, the default DH groups for newly created IPsec configurations are changed from groups 14 and 5 to groups 20 and 21.The upgrade behavior depends on whether the existing DH groups were explicitly configured or were using the legacy default values.The following table summarizes the behavior.Configuration scenarioDH groups after upgrade or creationNewly created IPsec configuration20, 21Existing configuration using the legacy default 14, 520, 21, 14Existing configuration with explicitly configured DH groupsExisting configured values are retainedThis change applies to both Phase 1 and Phase 2 IPsec configurations.For example:An existing configuration using the legacy default 14 5 is updated to include 20 21 14.An existing configuration explicitly using 5 remains 5.Existing configurations with other DH-group combinations, such as 20 5, retain their configured values.The distinction between default and explicitly configured values is important when assessing the impact of a firmware upgrade.Understand Phase 1 and Phase 2 DH-group negotiation.Phase 1 and Phase 2 use DH groups for different key exchange operations.Phase 1:During Phase 1, the VPN peers negotiate the IKE SA parameters, including the encryption algorithm, integrity algorithm, PRF, and DH group.The configured Phase 1 DH-group lists must have at least one mutually supported group for the peers to establish the IKE SA.Phase 2:Phase 2 establishes the IPsec SA used to protect user traffic.When Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) is enabled, an additional DH exchange is performed for the Phase 2 key material. The configured Phase 2 DH-group lists must therefore have at least one mutually supported group.When PFS is disabled, there is no separate Phase 2 DH exchange.Important: Phase 1 and Phase 2 DH groups do not need to be identical. Each phase has its own DH-group negotiation requirements.For example, Phase 1 can use DH group 20 while Phase 2 uses DH group 14, provided the corresponding VPN peers have compatible configurations.Verify DH-group compatibility between VPN peersAfter upgrading FortiOS, verify the DH-group configuration on both VPN peers.Run the following commands to inspect the Phase 1 and Phase 2 configurations.show full-configuration vpn ipsec phase1-interface show full-configuration vpn ipsec phase2-interfaceCheck the following parameters:Phase 1 DH groups on both peers.Phase 2 DH groups on both peers.Whether PFS is enabled or disabled.Whether the configured DH groups are supported by the remote VPN device.Whether at least one mutually supported DH group exists for each applicable negotiation.The DH-group lists on both peers do not necessarily need to be identical. They must have at least one common supported group for the relevant exchange.Compatible DH-group configuration:Local FortiGate:config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit "VPN-TUNNEL" set dhgrp 20 14 next endRemote VPN peer:config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit "VPN-TUNNEL" set dhgrp 14 5 next endIn this example, both peers support DH group 14. Therefore, the Phase 1 DH-group configuration has a common supported group even though the configured lists are different.The same compatibility principle applies to Phase 2 when PFS is enabled.Consider the impact of PFS on Phase 2.Phase 2 DH-group compatibility must be evaluated separately from Phase 1. For example, the following configuration uses different DH groups for the two phases.Local FortiGate:config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit "VPN-TUNNEL" set dhgrp 20 14 next end config vpn ipsec phase2-interface edit "VPN-TUNNEL-P2" set phase1name "VPN-TUNNEL" set pfs enable set dhgrp 21 20 next endRemote VPN peer:config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit "VPN-TUNNEL" set dhgrp 14 5 next end config vpn ipsec phase2-interface edit "VPN-TUNNEL-P2" set phase1name "VPN-TUNNEL" set pfs enable set dhgrp 20 14 next endIn this example: Phase 1 has DH group 14 in common. Phase 2 has DH group 20 in common. The Phase 1 and Phase 2 DH-group lists are different. Both phases have a mutually supported group for their respective exchangesIf PFS is disabled, no separate Phase 2 DH-group negotiation is required.Recommended checks before and after upgrading:Before upgrading FortiOS:Review the Phase 1 and Phase 2 DH-group configurations.Identify tunnels using the legacy default DH groups 14 and 5.Identify tunnels with explicitly configured DH groups.Verify that the remote VPN peers support the DH groups that will be offered after the upgrade.Review VPN

topics.title: LDAP Connection through ZTNA tunnel from FortiAuthenticator Cloud fails due to "Certificate Unknown"
topics.summary: DescriptionThe connectivity failure observed when accessing the LDAP server behind FortiGate from FortiAuthenticator ('FAC') Cloud via a Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) tunnel.ScopeFortiOS.FortiAuthenticator.SolutionTo configure the ZTNA access to the LDAP server from FortiAuthenticator, refer to this document: Accessing an AD server with a zero trust tunnel on FortiAuthenticator.The following errors are observed on FortiAuthenticator when trying to query for group information.Sample error 1:As observed in the packet capture taken on the FortiGate (FGT), the TLS handshake fails with a "Certificate Unknown" alert sent from the FortiAuthenticator (FAC) end.Sample error 2:For the ZTNA server certificate, the self-signed certificate generated on the FortiGate (FGT) was used. The corresponding Sub-CA and CA certificates were uploaded to FortiAuthenticator (FAC) to establish the certificate trust chain. However, despite importing these certificates, the same TLS handshake failure with a "Certificate Unknown" alert from the FAC end continues to occur.Resolution:It is recommended to use either a public CA-signed certificate or a FortiAuthenticator (FAC) local CA-signed certificate as the ZTNA server certificate on the FortiGate (FGT), instead of using the self-signed certificate generated by the FGT. This ensures proper certificate chain validation and avoids TLS handshake failures due to certificate trust issues.

The article provides a step-by-step solution to resolve this issue.ScopeFortiGate, FortiManager, FortiExtender.SolutionWhen trying to upgrade an ADOM that has FortiExtender in it, FortiManager can give an error as below:Fail (errno=171): Package copy failed. object: fortiextender. detail: failed to copy 756-3:Run the following debug command first on FortiManager CLI, and try to upgrade the ADOM, to identify the issue exactly:diagnose debug enable diagnose debug service dvmdb 255If there is an output similar to this, then the ADOM upgrade is failing due to FortiExtender values in FortiManager DB. This error is caused by FortiExtender that sends unsupported characters for '_cid', and '_apn' values. __do_cdb_node_attr_check error:_gsm_profile._apn У̿ --> commit ocate: 4026] copy _gsm_profile.(soid=10916) to dparent=29505, fail: err=-999,The string contains XSS vulnerability characters - prop-_apn]: string(У̿) ======= Dump sentry and dentry====== 10916 ---> 29507 _cid: ѣ̿ ---> ѣ̿ _apn: У̿ ---> У̿ =================================== =cate: 4026] copy _gsm_profile.(soid=10916) to dparent=29505, :fail. 5cate: 4024] copy _modem1.(soid=10914) to dparent=10912, :fail. 2cate: 3228] copy extension-controller extender.FEX511F(soid=10912) to dparent=10911, :fail. __upgrade_one_adom,4574: reap child 24369 (r = 255)To resolve the issue, follow these steps: Disable dynamic update for FortiExtender from FortiGate by running the following command on FortiManager CLI:config system dm set fortiap-refresh-itvl 0 endRemove the FortiExtender dynamic data in ADOM by running the following command on FortiManager CLI:diagnose dvm extender reset-adom Upgrade the ADOMSet the default value for 'fortiap-refresh-itvl’ back by running the following command on FortiManager CLI:config system dm unset fortiap-refresh-itvl end

topics.title: Blank page when accessing FortiGate remote management via FortiManagement Cloud version 26.3a with custom HTTPS port
topics.summary: DescriptionRemote access to a FortiGate device from FortiManagement Cloud results in a blank page when a custom administration port is configured.ScopeFortiGate, FortiManagement Cloud.SolutionSymptoms.When using FortiManagement Cloud to remotely access a FortiGate device that has a custom HTTPS administration port (e.g., 4443) configured, the remote access page remains blank. The FortiManagement Cloud API incorrectly reports the administration port as 443 instead of the configured custom port.Root cause.This is a known issue in FortiManagement Cloud version 26.3.a where the system fails to correctly identify and use the custom administration port of the managed FortiGate device for remote access sessions.Resolution.Workaround.Change the FortiGate HTTPS administration port back to the default port 443. This allows FortiManagement Cloud to establish the remote access session correctly.Permanent fix.The issue is addressed in version 26.4 and correctly supports custom administration ports for remote access. This version is expected to be released in the first week of November 2026.

topics.title: Technical Tip: Exclude few config to sync between HA members with 'vdom-exception'
topics.summary: Description This article explains excluding a few configs to sync between HA units. Scope FortiGate.Solution When FortiGate in HA with config sync enabled, if few config needs to be exempted to sync with HA members. When both the FortiGate are in different availability zone (Cloud), both the FortiGate will have different subnets for each interfaces, so interface IP config should not sync with FortiGate member. Similarly, if any other config should be excluded from sync. To exclude the config to sync enable the Vdom-Exception. Note: In Azure HA scenarios, it is essential to manually set the physical interface IP address (e.g., port1) and local tunnel interface IP addresses on the secondary FortiGate. HA does not automatically synchronize these IP addresses. Additionally, the loopback interface configuration must be copied manually from the HA primary to the secondary FortiGate. Configuring a VDOM exception for 'system.interface' does not affect behavior. CLI example to configure the Vdom-Exception. config sys vdom-exception edit set object nextend Below is the example to exclude the interface and Static route config sync between HA members: config system vdom-exception edit 1 set object system.interface next edit 2 set object router.static nextend Note.Config which are part of 'vdom-exception' should be manually configured on both the FortiGates. topics.title: FortiGate provisioned through FortiManager ZTP stays unregistered with FortiCare for hours
topics.summary: DescriptionA FortiGate provisioned through the FortiManager ZTP workflow can remain unregistered with FortiCare for 30 minutes to several hours, even though the FortiCare portal shows valid contracts. This article describes the symptoms, the cause, and the workarounds for the delay.ScopeAll FortiGate models running FortiOS version 7.4.x or above, provisioned through ZTP by FortiManager.SolutionSymptoms.After a FortiGate is provisioned through the FortiManager ZTP workflow, the device does not reach registered status for 30 minutes, several hours, or in some cases until the next day. The device eventually registers on its own, but the delay blocks the remainder of the deployment. The issue is intermittent, and not every device in the same deployment is affected.The following conditions are present:FortiCare portal: the serial number is registered correctly, and the contracts are valid.FortiGuard updates: database updates work normally. The update debug output shows that the FDS endpoint is reachable, Server certificate OK, a good OCSP status, and do_update[750]-UPDATE successful.Contract information: the contract is installed, but the account association is missing, as shown in the following output:diagnose test update info contract Support contract: pending_registration=255 got_contract_info=1 account_id=[] company=[] industry=[]FortiManager: the device is shown as unregistered with FortiCare and is placed in the Unregistered Devices group.Cause.No single root cause is confirmed. The behavior results from the interaction of the following three factors:Server-side readiness delay: the FortiGate installs the contract (FSCI000(contract) installed successfully), but the account_id value is not yet populated on the FDS side. The FDS servers hold the registration information for the affected serial numbers, so the delay is a timing window and not a missing entitlement.Daily auto-update schedule: the default auto-update schedule for new FortiGate devices changed from approximately every 20 to 30 minutes to daily. Without a configuration change, a reboot, or a manual execute update-now, the FortiGate has no reason to issue a new update request. It therefore does not check again whether the server-side account data is ready.FortiManager restriction: starting with FortiManager 7.6.7, the RTM daemon queries the license status of each managed FortiGate every 3 minutes. When account_id is empty, FortiManager flags the device as FC_UNREG and moves it to the Unregistered with FortiCare device group. Policy installation and CLI script push are blocked for devices in this group.While the updater waits for server-side contract data, the update debug output shows the following message. The freeze interval is 60 minutes.Online Update freezed, expiry=yyy, current=xxxThese factors create a circular dependency:The FortiGate does not register automatically within an acceptable timeframe.FortiManager detects the device as unregistered (FC_UNREG).FortiManager blocks policy installation and CLI script push.The FortiGuard configuration workaround cannot be pushed remotely.The ZTP deployment stalls, and the device remains unmanaged until it registers on its own.Resolution.No confirmed fix is available. Apply one of the following workarounds according to the access available to the FortiGate.When console or CLI access is available, change the FortiGuard settings. This is the fastest and most reliable workaround because the change triggers an update request and the registration completes within minutes.config system fortiguard set fortiguard-anycast disable set protocol udp set port 8888 set sdns-server-ip 208.91.112.220 173.243.140.53 210.7.96.53 200.91.112.220 end execute update-nowVerify the registration with the following command. The account_id, company, and industry values are now populated.diagnose test update info contractWhen console access is not available, register the FortiGate with FortiCloud before provisioning. Register it at least 1 hour in advance, with 20 to 30 minutes as the practical minimum, and then reboot the FortiGate. The reboot forces the contract update check that the daily auto-update schedule would otherwise defer.As another option, add the FortiGuard configuration to a Pre-Run CLI template in FortiManager. Go to Device Manager -> Provisioning Templates -> CLI Templates, and create a Pre-Run CLI template with the following configuration. Assign the template to the model device when adding it.config system fortiguard set fortiguard-anycast disable set protocol udp set port 8888 set sdns-server-ip 208.91.112.220 173.243.140.53 210.7.96.53 200.91.112.220 endDo not include execute update-now in the Pre-Run CLI template.Note: This workaround is effective only when the template is applied before FortiManager flags the device as FC_UNREG. While the FortiGate is in the Unregistered Devices group, FortiManager cannot push configuration through the model device workflow.To confirm the FortiGuard connectivity and the up

Be patient.Once the log creation is complete, the 'Download' button will appear. Download the log. topics.title: Technical Tip: SD-WAN ADVPN 2.0 - load-balancing traffic over multiple shortcuts
topics.summary: Description This article describes the configuration needed to have traffic load-balanced over multiple shortcuts for ADVPN SD-WAN 2.0 Scope Available from FortiOS 7.6.0 Solution The load-balancing of traffic over several shortcuts will be effective when the following configuration is applied: config system sdwan config service edit 1 set load-balance enable set mode sla … set tie-break fib-best-match next end With the above configuration, the source spoke will establish and use a full mesh of shortcuts between all local members and all members of the remote spoke within the same transport-group. The transport-group is configured at the SD-WAN member level. The algorithm used for load balancing is defined (once load-balance is enabled for this service) by: config system sdwan config service edit 1 set hash-mode For details of the different hash-modes available, see 'load balance hash methods' section of the documentation. Configuring load-balance with a manual service (config service, set mode manual) will result in only one shortcut being created in release 7.6.0.

topics.title: FortiAP CAPWAP AP-leave/join behavior with reason "AP DTLS peer disconnected"
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiAP CAPWAP AP-leave/join behavior with reason "AP DTLS peer disconnected".ScopeAffected products and versions:FortiAP 7.6.4FortiGate 7.4.11A FortiAP managed on the FortiGate FirewallSolutionThis particular type of FortiAP CAPWAP AP-leave/join error, "AP DTLS peer disconnected" with message "CWWE_DC_DEAD_INTERVAL_EXPIRE(103) new DTLS_TD(13)" typically occurs when the FortiAP does not get a CAPWAP Keepalive response from the uplink Network (Switch/FortiGate):date=2026-03-03 time=14:47:30 eventtime=177252944964231XXXX tz="+0530" logid="010404XXXX" type="event" subtype="wireless" level="notice" vd="root" logdesc="Physical AP leave" sn="FP231FTF2300XXXX" ap="AP01" profile="231F" ip=172.16.104.53 meshmode="mesh root ap" snmeshparent="N/A" action="ap-leave" reason="AP DTLS peer disconnected" msg="AP AP01 left." 1661.713 AC0,1 FSM0:old RUN(22) ev CWWE_DC_DEAD_INTERVAL_EXPIRE(103) new DTLS_TD(13)To identify if the cause of the CAPWAP re-join issue is related to the FortiAP, FortiGate, or the Network, the CAPWAP debug logs will be needed from both the FortiAP and the FortiGate. Additionally, switch port-mirror captures are required from the uplink switch port of the FortiAP and FortiGate during the problem state to determine if the FortiGate is receiving CAPWAP keepalives from the FortiAP and to confirm whether the FortiAP is sending the CAPWAP keepalives to the uplink Switch/FortiGate.Typical causes of the "AP DTLS peer disconnected" error:When the FortiAP/SSIDs/Wired Network are all on the same flat network, this may add network congestion between the FortiAP and the FortiGate, which might cause CAPWAP keepalive misses.On the affected FortiAP, verify if the User has misconfigured "AC_IPADDR" with an IP address outside the FortiAP subnet/VLAN for a static FortiGate WiFi Controller discovery. If so, it can result in CAPWAP leave/join behavior. Therefore, match the FortiGate AC IP address to the FortiAP VLAN/subnet on the FortiAP.Use the following commands to view the current "AC_IPADDR" setting on the FortiAP and correct the config accordingly:cfg -s cfg -a AC_IPADDR_1= cfg -cRelated Articles:FortiAP CLI configuration commandsFortiAP WiFi Controller discovery methodsFortiAP exhibits AP-leave/join behavior on the FortiGateHow to collect logs and config to assist TAC in debugging issues on FortiAP WiFi

topics.title: ZTNA destination access is slow when IPv6 is enabled on the Windows network adapter
topics.summary: DescriptionConnections to ZTNA destinations over RDP or HTTP take 10 to 20 seconds when IPv6 is enabled on the network adapter of a Windows endpoint running FortiClient. This article describes the symptoms, the cause, and the workarounds.ScopeFortiClient 7.4.7 and 7.4.9 for Windows with ZTNA enabled, managed by FortiClient EMS, connecting to FQDN-based destinations through a FortiGate ZTNA access proxy.SolutionSymptomsConnection delay: connecting to a ZTNA destination over RDP or HTTP takes 10 to 20 seconds.DNS behavior: nslookup for the ZTNA destination FQDN times out or returns a non-existent domain response.IPv6 dependency: disabling IPv6 on the network adapter of the endpoint reduces the connection time to approximately 1 second.Unaffected destinations: destinations configured with literal IP addresses do not trigger a DNS lookup and are not affected.CauseFortiClient intercepts ZTNA traffic for FQDN-based destinations through a DNS proxy. An IPv6 DNS server bypasses this proxy, so FortiClient blocks IPv6 DNS queries by design while ZTNA is active. ZTNA does not currently support IPv6 DNS resolution.The Windows DNS client sends the query over IPv6 first, waits for a retry timeout of approximately 10 seconds, and then falls back to IPv4. This wait produces the delay.The FortiClient diagnostic logs confirm the condition with entries similar to the following.Block IPV6 DNS query: remoteIp=2001:db8::53 remotePort=53The limitation applies to DNS resolution over IPv6. It is not a general IPv6 addressing failure. The behavior is the same on FortiOS 7.4.8 and 7.6.7, which indicates a FortiClient limitation and not a FortiGate or FortiClient EMS configuration issue.ResolutionApply one of the following workarounds.To disable IPv6 on the affected network adapter, open PowerShell as an administrator and list the adapters that have the IPv6 binding enabled.Get-NetAdapterBinding -ComponentID ms_tcpip6Disable the IPv6 binding on the affected adapter. Replace Ethernet with the adapter name returned by the previous command.Disable-NetAdapterBinding -Name "Ethernet" -ComponentID ms_tcpip6To restore the IPv6 binding later, run the following command.Enable-NetAdapterBinding -Name "Ethernet" -ComponentID ms_tcpip6If IPv6 must remain enabled on the adapter, avoid IPv6 DNS resolution for the ZTNA destinations instead. Configure the ZTNA destinations with IP addresses instead of FQDNs, because a literal IP address does not trigger a DNS lookup. If FQDNs are required, configure the endpoints to use DNS servers that are reachable over IPv4 only.After applying either workaround, connect to the ZTNA destination again. The connection time is approximately 1 second.Note: The ipv6_dns_server_disable setting in the ZTNA profile XML on FortiClient EMS controls IPv6 DNS over UDP only. In testing, setting it to 1 did not remove the delay, and setting it to 0 stopped the ZTNA destinations from connecting until IPv6 was disabled on the adapter. Do not use this setting as a workaround for this issue.Related articlesZTNA Destinations in the FortiClient 7.4.0 EMS Administration GuideHow to resolve DNS issue with FortiClient SSL VPN when IPv6 is enabled on the client network adapter

topics.title: DHCP IP address assignment failure only on specific VLANs 97 and 98 on a Bridge mode SSID on the FortiAP-221E model
topics.summary: DescriptionDHCP IP address assignment failure only on specific VLANs 97 and 98 on a Bridge mode SSID on the FortiAP-221E model.ScopeFortiAP-221E 7.4.6, FortiGate 7.6.6.SolutionVLAN 97 and 98 are reserved for Internet use on the FortiAP-W2 models. Therefore, do not use those VLAN IDs in the FortiAP management VLAN, SSID static VLAN, and dynamically assigned VLAN. Refer to Reserved VLAN IDs.Since the FortiAP-221E is now a legacy model, and this behavior is as per the design and is expected on the E series FortiAP models, there are currently no plans to modify this functionality on this model. To move forward, consider either:Using alternative VLAN IDs instead of 97 and 98, or:Upgrading to a newer FortiAP model, as the current F, G, and K series FortiAPs support these VLAN IDs.

topics.title: Block Claude Chat while allowing other Claude features when using FortiGate as an explicit proxy
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to block Anthropic's Claude web chat feature while allowing other features, such as Code CLI, when FortiGate is running as an explicit proxy. In addition, it is possible to allow only the Chat feature via the Desktop App while blocking the web chat, which is also described in this article.ScopeFortiGate configured with the explicit proxy feature.SolutionAnthropic's Claude can be accessed using multiple clients, such as the Claude.ai web interface, the Claude Desktop App, and developer-oriented tools such as Claude Code CLI. If the security requirement for an organization is to allow programmatic API Access, while blocking the consumer-grade channels, this can be achieved on FortiGate by following these steps:Create a proxy address for .claude.ai:config firewall proxy-address edit ".claude.ai" set type host-regex set host-regex ".*claude\\.ai" next endUse a RegEx pattern to scope the block to the chat conversation path only.config firewall proxy-address edit "claude-chat" set host ".claude.ai" set path ".*\\/chat_conversations\\/.*" next endCreate a proxy policy on top of the ones allowing access to the rest of the traffic, and use the policy to block the traffic destined to claude-chat:Note:SSL deep inspection is required for this setup.config firewall proxy-policy edit set name "block-claude-chat" set proxy explicit-web set dstintf set srcaddr "LAN" set dstaddr "claude-chat" set service "webproxy" set schedule "always" set logtraffic all set ssl-ssh-profile "Deep_SSL_INSPECTION" next endThe steps above should block the traffic for the destination matching the claude-chat proxy address.Claude desktop uses a specific User-Agent header, which is .*Claude.*Electron.*So, to allow the Chat feature via the Desktop App while blocking it on the Web, use the following steps.Create a proxy address with a type header for specifying the user-agent:config firewall proxy-address edit "user-agent-claude" set type header set host "all" set header-name "user-agent" set header ".*Claude.*Electron.*" next endCreate a policy that blocks traffic destined for the Claude chat proxy address and does not have a user-agent header .*Claude.*Electron.* (proxy address: user-agent-claude) by enabling the source negate on the proxy policy.config firewall proxy-policy edit set name "block-claude-chat-Web" set proxy explicit-web set dstintf set srcaddr "user-agent-claude" set dstaddr "claude-chat" set service "webproxy" set srcaddr-negate enable set schedule "always" set logtraffic all set ssl-ssh-profile "Deep_SSL_INSPECTION" next end
topics.versionScope: FortiGate configured with the explicit proxy feature

topics.title: FortiGuard update installation failure caused by disk I/O errors on /dev/sda
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to troubleshoot a FortiGuard update failure where package downloads succeed, but the installation stage fails because of underlying disk I/O and filesystem errors on /dev/sda.In this scenario, FortiGuard communication can be operational and update packages can be downloaded successfully. However, the downloaded package cannot be installed because the FortiGate is experiencing I/O errors affecting the system disk.The key indicators are kernel messages similar to:print_req_error: I/O error, dev sda, sector 1 Buffer I/O error on dev sda1, logical block 0, async page read EXT2-fs (sda3): previous I/O error to superblock detected EXT2-fs (sda2): previous I/O error to superblock detectedThese errors can be observed in the console, COMLog, system event logs, or crashlog.ScopeAffects:FortiGate.FortiOS.FortiGuard update failures associated with disk or filesystem errors.SolutionSymptomsThe FortiGate may experience one or more of the following symptoms:FortiGuard IPS, AV, Application Control, or other security package updates do not complete.FortiGuard connectivity is working and the package download succeeds.The update process fails during the package installation stage.diagnose debug application update -1 may show failures while copying or writing files under system locations such as /etc or /data2.Line [411]: __upd_peer_vfy[334]-Server certificate OK. — SSL/TLS handshake succeeds, no cert errors. Line e432]: get_fcpr_responses298]-Unpacked obj: ... Response=300 ... ResponseItem=...:200 — FortiGuard returns HTTP 200 for most components (IPS, AV, etc.) Line i449]: installUpdObjRestR941]-Failed to copy new obj file /tmp/updLIMESH to /etc/fcni.dat, errno=2, No such file or directory — Line 488]: installUpdObjRestb898]-Failed to copy new sig file /tmp/upddJ7rvF.x to /etc/ips.et.rules.x, errno=2, No such file or directory Line 640]: install_Madbl2925]-fgunzip /tmp/updHmRgGE /data2/madb.dat ret -2 Line 656]: upd_install_pkgl1467]-Failed to install FCNI000(fcni) result=(-12,0). Line 680]: upd_status_save_statuss193]-Failed writing /etc/upd.dat Line 682]: __upd_act_updateu310]-Failed installing pkg — the update is aborted. Line /985]: do_updateo690]-UPDATE failed — final result.Messages such as the following may be observed:errno=2, No such file or directory Failed writing /etc/upd.dat upd_install_pkg failed UPDATE failedAt the same time, console, COMLog, or crashlog output contains repeated and persistent I/O errors similar to the following:Run:diagnose debug crashlog readSearch for recurring filesystem or disk I/O messages.For example:print_req_error: I/O error, dev sda, sector 1 print_req_error: I/O error, dev sda, sector 1 Buffer I/O error on dev sda1, logical block 0, async page readAdditional filesystem errors may be present:EXT2-fs (sda3): previous I/O error to superblock detected EXT2-fs (sda2): previous I/O error to superblock detectedRoot causeThe FortiGuard update failure in this scenario was ultimately isolated to disk I/O errors and once the disk I/O error was diagnosed and resolved, the FortiOS was able to install the updates properly.Information to collect for a Fortinet TAC caseIf the issue persists, collect at minimum:get system status get hardware status get system storage execute disk list diagnose hardware deviceinfo disk diagnose debug crashlog readAlso provide:COMLog/console.FortiGuard update debug output showing the package download and installation failure.Approximate timestamp when the FortiGuard update failed.HA status, if applicable.

topics.title: FortiNDR ML training status shows Training on Hold after upgrade to 7.6.4
topics.summary: DescriptionMachine Learning training fails to establish a baseline and displays a Training on Hold status following an upgrade from FortiNDR version 7.4.10 to 7.6.4.ScopeFortiNDR.SolutionSymptomsAfter upgrading FortiNDR from version 7.4.10 to 7.6.4, the following issues occur:The ML training status displays "Training on Hold (no active sensor in this sensor group...)".The completion time for ML training is incorrect.Sensors may appear to be removed from the ML training group.Database errors are present in the system logs.Root CauseDuring the upgrade from version 7.4.10, a SQL statement execution error occurs. This prevents subsequent SQL statements from executing, which results in the ML baseline and training data not being migrated or created correctly. Consequently, the system cannot establish a baseline even though ML training is automatically triggered after the upgrade. ResolutionTo resolve this issue and ensure a successful upgrade, follow these steps:While the system is still running FortiNDR version 7.4.10, run the following command to clear existing ML Discovery logs and reset the ML database:exec cleanup mlPerform the upgrade following the supported path: 7.4.10 -> 7.6.3 -> 7.6.4.After the upgrade, verify that the ML training is running correctly and the Baseline Status no longer shows "Training on Hold".Additional InformationRunning the CLI command below clears all existing FortiNDR ML Discovery logs. This makes the current baseline outdated, and the system will automatically retrain a new baseline. This action does not affect data sessions but resets the ML database.exec cleanup mlBy default, ML retraining completes within one week. To reduce the training time, use the following command:exec reset-ml-baseline-time ndr

topics.title: Zip file downloads blocked when Antivirus profile is in Proxy mode with stream scan
topics.summary: DescriptionZip file downloads are blocked on FortiGate version 8.0.0 when the Antivirus profile is configured in Proxy mode and uses stream scan.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptoms.Zip file downloads are blocked when the following conditions are met:• The FortiGate runs version 8.0.0.• The Antivirus profile is configured in Proxy mode.• The scan mode is set to stream scan (default setting).Root cause.Bug ID 1260804 in FortiGate version 8.0.0 causes ZIP file downloads to be blocked when the Antivirus profile uses stream scan in Proxy mode.Resolution.Option 1: Upgrade FortiGate.Upgrade the FortiGate to version 8.0.1 or later to resolve this issue.Resolved Issues 8.0.1Option 2: Workaround.Change the Antivirus scan mode from stream scan to legacy scan if an upgrade is not immediately possible.Open the Command Line Interface (CLI).Run the following commands to change the scan mode to legacy:config antivirus profile edit set scan-mode legacy next end

topics.title: Intermittent SSL/TLS failures on website portals with Deep SSL Inspection and IPS (flow-based) — blank page / ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR
topics.summary: DescriptionWhen a firewall policy runs flow-based inspection with Deep SSL Inspection and an IPS sensor, an HTTPS application can intermittently fail mid-session.Scope FortiOS 7.6.7.SolutionSymptomsUsers may experience intermittent failures when loading or submitting content on specific websites, resulting in a blank page.The browser may report net::ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR, with the failed request showing:Status = 0No HTTP versionNo server IP addressNo response bytes receivedFortiGate SSL inspection logs indicate that the affected sessions are otherwise processed successfully, including:action="accept" and utmaction="allow"Successful SSL/TLS handshake completion (handshake-done)mitm="yes" indicating successful deep inspectionA valid server certificateIn some cases, traffic flows terminate with action="client-rst" while utmaction="allow" remains unchanged.IPS debugging shows that the corresponding session is finalized (ips_tcp_layer_fini) during an idle period. When the client subsequently attempts to close or reuse the same connection, the IPS engine can no longer locate the associated session. topics.title: Fields missing in Antivirus Log ID 8195 when using Content-Type: multipart/form-data
topics.summary: DescriptionCertain fields are missing from Antivirus logs (Message ID 8195) when the HTTP Content-Type is multipart/form-data and proxy-based inspection is used.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptoms.When using proxy-based inspection for HTTP or HTTPS traffic with a multipart/form-dataContent-Type, the Antivirus logs (Message ID 8195 for monitored actions and Message ID 8194 for blocked actions) do not contain the following fields:agent.httpmethod.referralurl.This issue only affects the log information and does not impact the actual Antivirus detection, monitoring, blocking, or traffic flow.Root cause.Bug ID 1281140 (Resolved issues) in FortiOS causes these specific fields to be omitted from the log output when the traffic is processed using proxy-based inspection and contains multipart form data.Resolution.Affected versions:FortiOS version 7.6.6.FortiOS version 8.0.0.Resolved versions:FortiOS version 7.6.7.FortiOS version 8.0.1.Resolved issues 8.0.1Resolved issues 7.6.7Upgrade the FortiGate to FortiOS version 7.6.7 or FortiOS version 8.0.1.Workaround.If an upgrade is not immediately possible, change the firewall policy inspection mode from proxy-based to flow-based. This issue does not occur in flow-based inspection mode.CLI configuration:config firewall policy edit set inspection-mode flow next endImportant:Before changing the inspection mode, review the security profiles applied to the firewall policy and verify their compatibility with flow-based inspection.

topics.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient IPsec IKEv2 VPN with SAML authentication with FortiIdentity as IdP, fails with 'Failed SAML cache group matching'
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to resolve the failure of a FortiClient IPsec IKEv2 remote access VPN connection that uses SAML authentication with FortiIdentity, where the SAML login succeeds but the FortiGate denies the user with the message 'Failed SAML cache group matching'.ScopeFortiGate, FortiIdentity.SolutionSymptoms.When connecting with FortiClient to a FortiGate IPsec IKEv2 remote access VPN that uses SAML authentication with FortiIdentity, the SAML login completes successfully in the browser, but the tunnel is not established. FortiClient reports an authentication failure. FortiIdentity returns StatusCode: Success, and the FortiGate debug output shows that the SAML assertion is accepted, but the user is denied during group matching:fnbamd_saml_auth_cache_lookup-Authentication passed. fnbam_user_auth_group_match-req id: ..., server: FortiIdentity, local auth: 0, dn match: 0 __group_match-Check if FortiIdentity is a group member handle_req-Failed SAML cache group matching. fnbamd_comm_send_result-Sending result 1 ike ... EAP ... result FNBAM_DENIED ike: EAP failed for user "user1" ike: connection expiring due to EAP failureA secondary message, 'EAP-TTLS/PAP: Invalid user password', may also appear. This message is a consequence of the denial and does not indicate a password problem.Cause.The FortiGate user group used by the VPN is configured with a config match entry. In this mode, the FortiGate compares the value of the group attribute in the SAML assertion (for example) with the group-name configuration in the match entry. The SAML username is used only as the identity of the user and is never compared with group-name. Setting group-name to a username, such as user1, always fails.The failure occurs in any of the following cases:Missing group attribute: FortiIdentity does not send a group attribute in the assertion, or the attribute is empty. This happens when the user does not belong to any group.Value mismatch: the value of the group attribute does not exactly match the group-name configuration in the config match entry of the FortiGate user group. The comparison is case-sensitive.Attribute name mismatch: the attribute name defined in the attribute mapping of FortiIdentity does not exactly match the group-name configured under config user saml on the FortiGate, for example, group instead of Groups. The comparison is case-sensitive.In the FortiGate GUI, the user group has the SAML server as a member and a match entry for the group. Go to User & Authentication -> User Groups to review the group.Resolution.Enable debug and reproduce the connection to collect the SAML assertion and the group matching result:diagnose debug reset diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose vpn ike log filter name diagnose debug application ike -1 diagnose debug application fnbamd -1 diagnose debug application samld -1 diagnose debug enablediagnose vpn ike log filter name: limits the IKE debug output to the specified phase 1 tunnel name.After the test, disable the debug:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug resetIn the samld output, inspect the saml:AttributeStatement element of the assertion and confirm whether a group attribute is present and which value it carries. Compare that value with the group-name match entry of the user group:show user group Group1 config user group edit "Group1" set member "FortiIdentity" config match edit 1 set server-name "FortiIdentity" set group-name "Group1" next end next endTwo options resolve the issue. Option A keeps the group match and requires FortiIdentity to send a matching group attribute. Option B removes the match entry and accepts any user authenticated by the SAML server.Option A: match on the group attribute. In FortiIdentity, go to Applications -> SSO, edit the SAML application, and select the Attribute Mapping tab. Configure the attribute mapping to send the value of the MemberOf attribute named Groups. The value must match the FortiGate group name, such as Group1. Assign the user to that group.On the FortiGate, confirm that the group-name of the SAML server definition is the name of the attribute sent by FortiIdentity:config user saml edit "FortiIdentity" set group-name "Groups" next endThen confirm that the match entry of the user group, shown in the output above, contains the exact value sent in the attribute. The two group-name settings are used as follows:config user saml -> group-name: the name of the attribute in the assertion that carries the group value. The name must match the attribute name defined in the attribute mapping of FortiIdentity.config match -> group-name: the value of the group attribute that is accepted. The value must match the value sent by FortiIdentity exactly, including the case.Without attribute mapping, FortiIdentity sends the group membership in the attribute MemberOf. In that case, set group-name to MemberOf under config user saml.Option B: accept any user from the SAML server. Remove the match entry so that the server-level memb

topics.title: Technical Tip: How to configure Network ID for distinguishing IKEv2 IPsec VPN tunnels using FortiClient XML file
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article explains how to edit the FortiClient XML file to distinguish multiple IKEv2 IPsec VPN tunnels using Network ID instead of Peer ID.ScopeFortiGate, FortiClient.SolutionWhen multiple dial-up IPsec IKEv2 IPsec VPN tunnels are configured on FortiGate, a unique Network ID must be defined on each Phase 1 configuration. This allows FortiGate to correctly match incoming IKEv2 initiations with the appropriate tunnel.If the Network ID is not defined, FortiGate cannot reliably determine which Phase 1 configuration to use when multiple IKEv2 dial‑up tunnels reside on the same interface. This behavior differs from IKEv1, where Peer IDs were used to distinguish between tunnels. Use the following CLI syntax to define the Network ID for each Phase 1 configuration: config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit " " set ike-version 2 set network-overlay enable set network-id next end The Network ID must be defined on both the FortiGate Phase1 and the FortiClient configuration to ensure correct tunnel matching.Note: The Network ID setting cannot be configured on unmanaged or standalone Forticlient. For managed Forticlient, configuration of Network ID is supported through Forticlient EMS starting with versions 7.2.6 and later or 7.4.1 and later.The FortiClient XML configuration file can be manually edited or provisioned via EMS with the Network ID attribute. Locate the section of the XML, and insert the tag as shown below.Note: Occasionally, this value is not included in the configuration. In that case, manually add the section as shown below. 2 2 In this example, '2' represents the Network ID and must match the corresponding Phase 1 configuration on the FortiGate.Ensure that the tag is placed within the correct tunnel definition block in the XML file.Result:After importing the modified XML configuration into FortiClient, the IKEv2 initiator message will include the Network ID.This allows FortiGate to correctly match the proper Phase 1 configuration even when multiple IKEv2 dial‑up tunnels share the same interface.The configured Network ID must be unique for each IKEv2 tunnel, allowing the FortiGate to distinguish and correctly select the intended Phase 1 configuration. topics.title: FortiToken Mobile registration and alert email failures on a FortiGate behind a restrictive perimeter firewall
topics.summary: DescriptionA FortiGate behind a perimeter firewall may be unable to register FortiToken Mobile licenses or send alert/activation email, even after a list of Fortinet IP addresses and ports is allow-listed. The fix is to allow the Fortinet FQDNs the FortiGate actually resolves and connects to (not a fixed set of IPs), make sure DNS resolution works, and point the FortiGate at a custom SMTP server if FortiCare support is not valid.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionThe email test fails:diagnose log alertmail test ... Cannot use fortinet-notifications.com when forticare support is invalid.The logs say the FortiGate cannot find the email server (log ID 0100020002):msg="Can't resolve the IP address of fortinet-notifications.com" msg="Can't resolve the IP address of fortinetvirussubmit.com" msg="Can't resolve the IP address of fortinetipssubmit.com"Token setup fails with error -7500:FortiGate was unable to communicate with FortiCloud. Provision token: FTKMOBxxxxxxxxxx error: -7500.When you add a token license in the GUI, it shows a red Internal Server Error message.The wrong addresses were allowed. The FortiGate talks to directregistration.fortinet.com and fortitokenmobile.fortinet.com. These names pointed to IP addresses that were not on the allow list. Fortinet IP addresses can change, so an allow list with only IP addresses will break again.DNS does not work. The FortiGate cannot turn fortinet-notifications.com into an IP address, so it has nowhere to send email.No valid support contract. The built-in Fortinet email server only works when the FortiGate has valid FortiCare support. Without it, you must use your own email server."Internal Server Error" and error -7500 only mean the FortiGate could not reach FortiCloud. diagnose fortitoken info may still say "reachable", so do not trust it alone.Run these commands on the FortiGate CLI.Ping the Fortinet names. If the name does not turn into an IP address, it is a DNS problem. If you get an IP address but no reply, the firewall is blocking it.show system dns execute ping directregistration.fortinet.com execute ping fortitokenmobile.fortinet.com execute ping fortinet-notifications.comCheck the tokens. If they show new and 0 are activated, the setup did not finish.diagnose fortitoken infoTest the email and read the error message.diagnose log alertmail testCapture the traffic to the IP address from step 1, then try the token setup again. Always put a real IP address in the filter, or the command fails.diagnose sniffer packet any "host 63.137.229.3" 4 0 aFollow the steps below to fix the issue:Use an internal or public email server if the FortiGate has no valid FortiCare support, or if the Fortinet email server is not reachable.For Gmail, use an app password.config system email-server set type custom set reply-to "fortigate@example.com" set server "smtp.example.com" set port 465 set authenticate enable set username "fortigate@example.com" set password set security smtps endFor port 587, use set security starttls.Add the token license again.Go to User & Authentication -> FortiTokens -> Create New -> Mobile Token and enter the activation code. Or use the CLI:execute fortitoken-mobile import

topics.title: Preventing BGP route advertisements between specific peers using communities
topics.summary: DescriptionSteps to prevent a FortiGate from advertising BGP routes learned from a specific neighbor to another BGP neighbor by using BGP communities and route maps.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionBy default, routes learned from one eBGP neighbor can be advertised to another eBGP neighbor.BGP communities can be used to identify routes received from a specific neighbor and filter their advertisements to another neighbor without maintaining individual prefix lists or relying on AS_PATH matching.Consider the following topology:DeviceAS numberBGP neighbor IPLocalFortiGate6500010.10.10.1, 10.10.20.1RemoteFortiGate16500110.10.10.2RemoteFortiGate26500210.10.20.2RemoteFortiGate1 advertises 172.16.1.0/24, and RemoteFortiGate2 advertises 172.16.2.0/24.The requirement is to prevent LocalFortiGate from advertising routes learned from RemoteFortiGate2 to RemoteFortiGate1 while retaining those routes locally.Before applying the filtering, RemoteFortiGate1 receives both prefixes:RemoteFortiGate1 # get router info bgp network Network Next Hop Metric LocPrf Weight RouteTag Path *> 172.16.1.0/24 0.0.0.0 100 32768 0 i *> 172.16.2.0/24 10.10.10.1 0 0 0 65000 65002 i Total number of prefixes 2Configure an inbound route map to assign a community to routes received from RemoteFortiGate2.config router route-map edit "TAG-FROM-PEER2" config rule edit 10 set action permit set set-community "65000:200" set set-community-additive enable next end next endThe set-community-additive enable setting preserves existing community values while adding 65000:200.Configure a community list to match the assigned community.config router community-list edit "FROM-PEER2" config rule edit 10 set action permit set match "65000:200" next end next endConfigure an outbound route map to deny routes matching the community list.config router route-map edit "FILTER-TO-PEER1" config rule edit 10 set action deny set match-community "FROM-PEER2" next edit 20 set action permit next end next endRule 10 denies routes matching community 65000:200. Rule 20 permits other eligible routes.Apply the route maps to the respective BGP neighbors on LocalFortiGate.config router bgp config neighbor edit "10.10.20.2" set route-map-in "TAG-FROM-PEER2" next edit "10.10.10.2" set route-map-out "FILTER-TO-PEER1" next end endRefresh the inbound and outbound BGP policies.Refresh routes received from RemoteFortiGate2:execute router clear bgp ip 10.10.20.2 soft inVerify that the community is assigned:LocalFortiGate # get router info bgp network 172.16.2.0/24 VRF 0 BGP routing table entry for 172.16.2.0/24 Paths: (1 available, best #1, table Default-IP-Routing-Table) Not advertised to any peer Original VRF 0 65002 10.10.20.2 from 10.10.20.2 (10.254.254.3) Origin IGP distance 20 metric 0, localpref 100, valid, external, best Community: 65000:200Refresh the outbound BGP policy toward RemoteFortiGate1:execute router clear bgp ip 10.10.10.2 soft outVerify that the routes are no longer advertised to RemoteFortiGate1.On LocalFortiGate:LocalFortiGate # get router info bgp neighbors 10.10.10.2 advertised-routes % No prefix for neighbor 10.10.10.2On RemoteFortiGate1:RemoteFortiGate1 # get router info bgp network Network Next Hop Metric LocPrf Weight RouteTag Path *> 172.16.1.0/24 0.0.0.0 100 32768 0 i Total number of prefixes 1RemoteFortiGate1 no longer receives 172.16.2.0/24.RemoteFortiGate2 continues to receive 172.16.1.0/24 from RemoteFortiGate1 through LocalFortiGate, confirming that the filtering is applied only in the intended direction.Note:An inbound BGP soft refresh may be required for existing routes to be reprocessed with the configured community.This method filters BGP paths carrying the assigned community. If another path to the same prefix becomes the best path without that community, it may still be advertised.Existing inbound or outbound route maps must be updated to incorporate these rules rather than replaced.The configuration was verified on FortiOS 7.6.7.Related articles:Stop advertising all routes learned from one BGP peer to other BGP peer(s)FortiGate BGP community lists

topics.title: FortiGate EMS fabric connector fails to validate CA certificate
topics.summary: DescriptionThe FortiClient/EMS fabric connector on FortiGate version 7.4.12 rejects a valid publicly signed FortiClient/EMS web server certificate with a CA not recognized error. This article describes the incident details, debugging, and solution of the issue.ScopeFortiGate, FortiClient EMS.SolutionAfter upgrading FortiOS, the FortiGate EMS fabric connector may fail to validate a valid EMS server certificate and display the error EMS server certificate is not signed by any known CA. The issue may occur even when the certificate chain is valid, and the required CA certificates are installed on the FortiGate. Also, it might be resolved after revalidating or reinstalling the certificate chain in the FortiGate certificate store. Enable the following debug commands, reproduce the issue by testing the EMS connection, and then disable debugging.diagnose debug reset diagnose debug application fcnacd -1 diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose endpoint filter show-large-data yes diagnose debug enableAfter reproducing the issue, stop debugging:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug resetThe message "Could not verify EMS cert chain" indicates that certificate-chain validation failed. The message "EMS server certificate is not signed by any known CA" points to a CA trust or certificate-validation failure, but does not by itself prove that the CA certificate is missing. Check the configured CA reference and whether the certificate chain is being validated correctly.The message "EMS verification data has changed on host or peer. Must reverify." indicates that the stored EMS verification information needs to be reviewed and reverified. Also check for "EMS CN does not match verified CN!", which indicates a mismatch between the configured verified common name and the certificate identity.If the TLS handshake completes only up to the server certificate and the FortiGate subsequently sends a TLS alert, investigate local certificate validation rather than assuming a network connectivity issue. Confirm the EMS hostname, certificate SAN, certificate validity, CA chain, and the verifying-ca, verified-cn, and certificate-fingerprint settings.Example output:2026-10-20 10:46:10 [ec_shm_find_safe:1615] PID:259, Number of total/missed query 40855400/0, ver:0, uid_sz:1024, expiry:556 2026-10-20 10:46:10 [__match_server_cert_key:486] Could not verify EMS cert chain. 2026-10-20 10:46:10 [__match_server_cert_key:560] ret=0 2026-10-20 10:46:10 [ec_ez_worker_process:400] Processing call for obj-id: 0, entry: "api/v1/system/serial_number" 2026-10-20 10:46:10 [_update_obj_stats:365] Storing (0, ems.xlab.si, 7) 2026-10-20 10:46:10 [ec_ez_worker_process:458] Call completed with failure. obj-id: 0, desc: "REST API to get EMS Serial Number.", entry: "api/v1/system/serial_number". error info: Error (-1@__generic_process_result_ex:148). EMS verification data has changed on host or peer. Must reverify. 2026-10-20 10:46:10 [ec_ez_worker_base_prep_resolver:383] Outgoing interface index 0 for 1 (ems.xlab.si). 2026-10-20 10:46:10 [ec_ez_worker_prep_data_url:190] Full URL: https://10.10.50.27/api/v1/settings/server/public_addressThe issue occurs when the EMS Fabric Connector retains stale certificate-verification settings. Specifically, the verified-cn and/or certificate-fingerprint fields may remain configured after the verifying-ca entry has been removed. This leaves the connector's certificate-verification configuration inconsistent, causing FortiGate to reject an otherwise valid EMS server certificate and display the error "EMS server certificate is not signed by any known CA".Workaround:Review the EMS connector configuration under "config endpoint-control fctems". If stale certificate verification settings are suspected, unset the certificate fingerprint and verified common name, then re-verify the EMS connection.config endpoint-control fctems edit 1 unset certificate-fingerprint unset verified-cn end endRelated Article:Troubleshooting Tip: Unable to connect FortiClient EMS due to a server certificate

topics.title: FortiNDR unresponsive with high memory usage after upgrade to version 7.6.4
topics.summary: DescriptionHow to troubleshoot high memory utilization that causes the FortiNDR web GUI and SSH access to become unresponsive or slow after upgrading to version 7.6.4.ScopeFortiNDR.SolutionSymptomsAfter upgrading to FortiNDR version 7.6.4, the following symptoms occur:Memory consumption spikes to critical levels (up to 99%).The web GUI is unresponsive.SSH sessions time out or drop with "Remote side unexpectedly closed network connection" errors.Root CauseThe PCAP dump feature is memory intensive. When enabled, it captures raw full packets for entire sessions, which can lead to high memory usage. If memory becomes exhausted, critical processes (such as the database handler) may be terminated by the system (Out of Memory killer), leaving the database in an inconsistent state and rendering the management interfaces unresponsive.ResolutionTo resolve the unresponsiveness and normalize memory usage, perform the following steps. Console access is required if SSH and GUI are non-functional.Connect to the FortiNDR via the console port.Run the reload command:execute reload Reboot the FortiNDR appliance.Run the following command to patch the database and ensure it is in a consistent state:diagnose system db Verify that the database patching process completes with hOK] for all entries. Memory usage should return to normal levels, and the GUI/SSH access should become responsive. Recommendations to Prevent RecurrenceSwitch to Payload Dump: In FortiNDR version 7.6.5, a new payload dump feature is introduced. This feature is more memory-efficient than PCAP dump because it extracts only the application layer payload of the packet that triggered the intrusion. Switch to payload dump once version 7.6.5 is available.Hardware Upgrade: If PCAP dump is required for business needs, contact the Fortinet sales team to upgrade the hardware to a model with more memory.

topics.title: FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer unable to access Internet
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes how to troubleshoot when FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer is unable to access the Internet.ScopeFortiManager and FortiAnalyzer.SolutionHow to check:At FortiManager, perform the following actions: execute ping google.com execute traceroute google.com execute traceroute 8.8.8.8From the results, FortiManager currently has 2 issues:Unable to translate the google.com URL into an IP address, which is related to a DNS issue.Unable to route out and reach 8.8.8.8, which is related to a routing issue.After that, at FortiManager, go to System Settings -> Network:Check the current DNS setting.Check the current Routing table setting.Solution:In FortiManager, configure a default route to resolve the routing issue.Commands to configure a static route from the FortiManager CLI:config system route edit 1 set device interfacename set gateway x.x.x.x next endIn FortiManager, configure the DNS settings to resolve the DNS issue.
