topics.title: Management interface access blocked when virtual patch and VRF are enabled
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiGate blocks GUI access to the management interface when virtual patching is enabled on a local-in policy and the management interface is configured with a VRF.This behavior exists in 7.6.6 and earlier versions.FGT_A # show sys interface port1 config system interface edit "port1" set vdom "vd1" set vrf 1 set ip 172.16.10.10 255.255.255.0 set allowaccess ping https ssh snmp http telnet set type physical set device-identification enable set device-user-identification disable set snmp-index 3 config ipv6 set ip6-allowaccess ping https ssh snmp end next end FGT_A # shshow firewall local-in-policy config firewall local-in-policy edit 1 set uuid 7c2f91b4-86e5-43a7-9d02-6135b8e4f0a6 set intf "port1" set srcaddr "all" set dstaddr "all" set action accept set service "ALL" set schedule "always" set virtual-patch enable next endScopeFortiGate.SolutionAfter disabling virtual-patch, GUI access will work immediately.FGT_A # config firewall local-in-policy FGT_A (local-in-policy) # edit 1 FGT_A (1) # set virtual-patch disable FGT_A (1) # endIf you unset VRF and then enable virtual-patch, GUI access can work as well:FGT_A # config sys interface FGT_A (interface) # edit port1 FGT_A (port1) # sh config system interface edit "port1" set vdom "vd1" set vrf 1 set ip 172.16.10.10 255.255.255.0 set allowaccess ping https ssh snmp http telnet set type physical set device-identification enable set device-user-identification disable set snmp-index 3 config ipv6 set ip6-allowaccess ping https ssh snmp end next end FGT_A (port1) # unset vrf FGT_A (port1) # end FGT_A # config firewall local-in-policy FGT_A (local-in-policy) # edit 1 FGT_A (1) # set virtual-patch enable FGT_A (1) # endThis behavior has a fix planned for FortiOS 8.0.3.

topics.title: Enabling a routing lookup (strict) for source verification for reply packets
topics.summary: DescriptionA new feature enables a routing lookup (strict) for reply packets.ScopeFortiGate v7.6.7, v8.0.0 and later.SolutionThe command set strict-src-check enable to enable strict Reverse Path Forwarding (RPF) checks does not cover the case of matching an existing session in the reply direction. The new command was introduced in FortiOS versions 7.6.7 and 8.0.0:config system settings set src-check-reply enable endenable: Enable source verification for reply packets.disable: Disable source verification for reply packets.The command src-check-reply helps prevent spoofed reply packets on FortiGate.

topics.title: CSRF validation error, SAML IdP Proxy with federated domains
topics.summary: Description An issue where users encounter a CSRF validation error when authenticating via SAML IdP Proxy with federated domains, such as Microsoft 365. Scope FortiAuthenticator. Solution When a user attempts to authenticate using a federated domain (for example, Microsoft 365) via the FortiAuthenticator SAML IdP Proxy, the process fails. The user is redirected from the identity provider back to the FortiAuthenticator endpoint /saml-idp-proxy/ and receives the following error message: Request failed CSRF validation: CSRF cookie not set. Refresh your browser and try again. This is a known issue in FortiAuthenticator version 6.6.10 and 8.0.3 which causes the system to fail to set the required CSRF token cookie during the SAML redirection process. When the browser performs the subsequent POST request to the login endpoint, the validation fails because the expected CSRF cookie is missing from the request headers. Resolution is to upgrade FortiAuthenticator to version 6.6.11, 8.0.4 or higher. This issue is resolved in firmware version 6.6.11 and 8.0.4. Internal engineering ticket ID is 1325777. topics.title: FortiSASE secure edge tunnel stays down after a FortiOS upgrade because of a Diffie-Hellman group mismatch
topics.summary: DescriptionFortiGate secure edge tunnel to FortiSASE stops negotiating after the FortiGate is upgraded to FortiOS 7.6.5, why the tunnel comes up when the Diffie-Hellman (DH) groups are set to 5 and 14 and then drops again with the groups back at 20 and 21, and how to fix the condition permanently.This article also explains why the tunnel settings on FortiManager are not the source of truth for this tunnel, and how to make the workaround persist on FortiOS builds that do not contain the code fix.ScopeFortiGate configured as a FortiSASE secure edge, FortiOS 7.6.5 and 7.6.6. FortiSASE. FortiManager used as the management station for the FortiGate. FortiOS 7.6.7 and later are not affected.SolutionSymptomA FortiGate operating as a FortiSASE secure edge has a VDOM, commonly named SASE, configured for LAN extension. The tunnel to the FortiSASE edge service is not created by an administrator. FortiOS creates and maintains it automatically, under a phase 1 interface named with the prefix ul-, for example ul-npu0_vlink1, and the interface carries the description "[fgconn] Do NOT edit. Automatically generated by extension controller".After the FortiGate is upgraded to FortiOS 7.6.5 or 7.6.6, the tunnel no longer establishes. The VPN logs show a large number of IKEv2 phase 1 proposals sent to the FortiSASE peer with no answer, each cycle ending in a negotiation timeout. The responder cookie in those log entries is all zeroes, which means the peer never replied. See the following logs for examples of Fortinet Tunnel ID, local IP, and interface names.date=2026-10-12 time=23:10:55 type=VPN subtype=tunnel action=tunnel-down vd=SASE vpntunnel="ul-npu0_vlink1" duration=28678 locip=172.16.10.90 remip=192.0.2.10 remport=4500 locport=4500 version="IKEv2" role="initiator" date=2026-10-12 time=23:17:46 type=VPN subtype=phase1 logid=0101037127 action=SA_INIT vpntunnel="ul-npu0_vlink1" status="success" locip=172.16.10.90 locport=4500 remip=192.0.2.10 remport=4500 outintf="npu0_vlink1" cookies="2999982861c3180a/0000000000000000" version="IKEv2" role="initiator" date=2026-10-12 time=23:18:03 type=VPN subtype=phase1 logid=0101037124 action=negotiate vpntunnel="ul-npu0_vlink1" status="fail" error="ike negotiation timeout" duration=15 date=2026-10-12 time=23:18:16 type=VPN subtype=tunnel logid=0101037142 action=auto_transport_switch vpntunnel="ul-npu0_vlink1" msg="switch auto transport from udp to tcp"The three entries repeat on a short cycle. In one hour of logs, a single FortiGate sent 109 IKEv2 phase 1 proposals to 192.0.2.10 and received no reply, and the same FortiGate logged 54 transport switches from UDP to TCP. No tunnel-up event appears after the initial drop.The second part of the symptom is the temporary fix. Setting the DH groups on the FortiGate to 5 and 14 brings the tunnel up. Some time later the tunnel drops, and the DH groups read 20 and 21 again. The FortiGate is not losing the change at random, as explained under "Why the configuration reverts".Root causeFortiOS 7.6.5 changed the default phase 1 and phase 2 DH group list from 14 and 5 to 20 and 21. The change is documented in the FortiOS 7.6.5 Release Notes, section Changes in default behavior. The FortiGate administration guide states the current default: by default, FortiGate uses DH group 20 and 21 when a VPN is configured from the GUI or CLI.FortiSASE continues to use DH groups 14 and 5 for this tunnel type, as documented in the FortiSASE deployment guides, section IPsec configuration. The tunnel created by the extension controller inherits the FortiOS default, which on FortiOS 7.6.5 and 7.6.6 is 20 and 21 with no other group in the list.The two ends therefore share no DH group. The FortiGate sends an IKEv2 IKE_SA_INIT proposal offering groups 20 and 21, the peer has no matching group, and the exchange never completes. The proposal payload in the IKE debug of an affected FortiGate contains the DH group values 0x14 (20) and 0x15 (21) only.The transport setting adds a second delay on top of the mismatch. These tunnels are created with transport set to auto. When the UDP attempt fails, FortiOS opens a TCP session to the peer on port 4500, and that session also fails, so each negotiation window is consumed before the FortiGate returns to UDP. The log entries with action auto_transport_switch and the IKE debug line 'auto transport timeout, use tcp port 4500' identify this behavior.Why the configuration revertsThe tunnel is an object owned by the FortiSASE connection controller on the FortiGate. When the controller re-creates the tunnel, it applies the FortiOS default DH group list, which replaces any manual change and any value that came from FortiManager. A tunnel reset on the FortiSASE side is enough to trigger that rebuild. This is why the tunnel comes up after the DH groups are set to 5 and 14, works for a period, and then drops with the groups back at 20 and 21.This also explains a common source of confusion when the FortiGate is managed by FortiManager. topics.title: Information required for FortiAppSec Cloud troubleshooting
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the essential information required when troubleshooting issues related to FortiAppSec Cloud. Providing the information outlined below helps Fortinet Support understand the issue, identify its scope, and investigate it more efficiently.ScopeFortiAppSec Cloud.SolutionRequired information.When opening a FortiAppSec Cloud support case, provide the following information:Application information.Application name.Application domain/FQDN.Affected URL(s) or specific application endpoints.Issue description.A clear and detailed description of the issue.Expected behavior and actual behavior.Exact error message or HTTP status code, if applicable.Date and time when the issue occurred.Scope and impact.Number of affected users (single user or multiple users).Impact across users, including whether all users or only specific users are affected.Scope of the issue, such as the entire application or specific pages, URLs, or functionalities.Frequency of occurrence (consistent or intermittent).Previous working status.Previous operational status of the application.Date and time when the issue was first observed.Application deployment status (newly onboarded application or existing application).Recent changes to the application, origin server, DNS, network, or FortiAppSec Cloud configuration before the issue started.Testing and reproduction.Steps required to reproduce the issue.Reproducibility results, including whether the issue occurs consistently or intermittently.Testing results from different browsers, devices, or networks, if available.Additional evidence.Depending on the nature of the issue, provide the following information and supporting evidence:Connectivity or performance issues: HAR files captured from both working and non-working scenarios, if available.Application errors: Screenshots and exact error messages displayed.Other issues: Relevant logs, screenshots, timestamps, or additional information that may help with the investigation.Note: HAR files may contain sensitive information, including session cookies, authentication tokens, and other credentials. Review and sanitize the files before sharing them with Fortinet Support.

topics.title: Error "Failed to save changes" while saving custom Application Control signature
topics.summary: DescriptionSteps to resolve the "Failed to save changes" error encountered when saving a custom Application Control signature.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionA syntax error can occur when saving a custom Application Control signature if the signature definition contains line breaks or formatting that prevents the parser from correctly interpreting the opening and closing parentheses.When attempting to save a custom Application Control signature, the GUI displays the error "Failed to save changes".To investigate the issue, run the following commands.diagnose debug disable diagnose debug reset diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose debug cli 8 diagnose debug cmdb-trace diagnose debug enableThe CLI and CMDB trace debug output indicates that the closing or opening parenthesis cannot be identified. This can occur when the signature definition is formatted across multiple lines in a way that the parser cannot recognize.kvm42 # 0: config application custom 0: edit "OutboundTSTServerCommunication" 0: set comment '' 0: set signature "F-SBID( 0: --attack_id 9901; 0: --name \"Outbound.TST.Server.Communication\"; 0: --default_action drop_session; 0: --service HTTP; 0: --protocol tcp; 0: --app_cat 25; 0: --flow from_client; 0: --pattern \"/.well-known/tst.json\"; 0: --context uri; 0: --no_case; 0: --weight 40; 0: )" 0: unset protocol 0: unset technology 0: unset behavior 0: unset vendor [error] line 1 offset 8: F-SBID( ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 2 offset 18: --attack_id 9901; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 3 offset 44: rver.Communication"; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 4 offset 31: action drop_session; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 5 offset 16: --service HTTP; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 6 offset 16: --protocol tcp; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 7 offset 14: --app_cat 25; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 8 offset 20: --flow from_client; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 9 offset 35: ell-known/mcp.json"; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 10 offset 15: --context uri; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 11 offset 11: --no_case; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 12 offset 13: --weight 40; ^^^ closing round bracket not found [error] line 13 offset 1: ) ^^^ open bracet not found -2: end The debug output reports syntax errors, including closing round bracket not found and open bracket not found. These errors indicate that the signature parser cannot correctly interpret the signature definition.To resolve the issue, enter the custom Application Control signature as a single continuous string, keeping the opening F-SBID( and closing ) within the same string and avoiding unnecessary line breaks.Navigate to the custom Application Control signature configuration in the FortiGate GUI and update the signature definition to use the following format.Select Save to apply the changes.The following debug output confirms that the signature is accepted, and the configuration is saved successfully.kvm42 # 0: config application custom 0: edit "OutboundTSTServerCommunication" 0: set comment '' 0: set signature "F-SBID( --attack_id 9901; --name \"Outbound.TST.Server.Communication\"; --default_action drop_session; --service HTTP; --protocol tcp; --app_cat 25; --flow from_client; --pattern \"/.well-known/tst.json\"; --context uri; --no_case; --weight 40; )" 0: unset protocol 0: unset technology 0: unset behavior 0: unset vendor 0: end [show_walker_construct:85] open('/tmp/system.conf.2285.xmxxc1) to save config of 'root' write config file success, prepare to save '/tmp/system.conf.2285.xmxxc1' to '/data/./config/sys_vd_root+root.conf.gz' on flash flash: block_sz=4096, free_blocks=23953 [__create_file_new_version:312] the new version config file '/data/./config/sys_vd_root+root.conf.gz.v000000024' is created [symlink_config_file:379] a new version of '/data/./config/sys_vd_root+root.conf.gz' is created: /data/./config/sys_vd_root+root.conf.gz.v000000024 [symlink_config_file:423] the old version '/data/./config/sys_vd_root+root.conf.gz.v000000023' is deleted [symlink_config_file:425] '/data/./config/sys_vd_root+root.conf.gz' has been symlink'ed to the new version '/data/./config/sys_vd_root+root.conf.gz.v000000024'. The o ld version '/data/./config/sys_vd_root+root.conf.gz.v000000023' has been deleted zip config file /data/./config/sys_vd_root+root.conf.gz success! topics.title: FortiManager firmware upgrade preview shows "No record found" even with an assigned device
topics.summary: DescriptionAn explanation for a "No record found" message occurring in the Firmware Upgrade Preview of a Firmware Template in FortiManager even when a device is assigned to the template. Steps to resolve it are provided.ScopeFortiManager.FortiGate.SolutionThe Firmware Upgrade Preview only lists devices that match the platform selected in the template. If the template platform is different from the platform of the assigned device, the preview has nothing to calculate and shows "No record found". No other error is shown, and the device still appears under "Assigned to Device/Group".This is easy to miss with virtual FortiGates, because several platform names look similar (for example FortiGate-VM64 and FortiGate-VM64-KVM).The device platform shows in the FortiGate CLI:FGT-SPOKE # get sys status Version: FortiGate-VM64-KVM v7.4.9,build2829,250924 (GA.M) First GA patch build date: 230509 Current Security Level: High Firmware Signature: certified Virus-DB: 1.00000(2018-04-09 18:07) Extended DB: 1.00000(2018-04-09 18:07) ....................... ............... .........The template platform is FortiGate-VM64, which does not match FortiGate-VM64-KVM.To avoid this, set the template Platform to "GA Versions" instead of a specific platform. The template is then not tied to one platform, and the Firmware Upgrade Preview selects the correct FortiGate platform for each assigned device.Go to Device Manager -> Firmware Templates and edit the template.In "Edit Upgrade Firmware", set Platform to "GA Versions".Select the target version under "Upgrade to".Save the template and open the Upgrade Preview.Related article:Troubleshooting Tip: Unable to select Setup Firmware Upgrade for FortiGate

topics.title: High packet drops occur during traffic bursts on a FortiGate VM hosted in Google Cloud Platform
topics.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the case when a FortiGate VM hosted on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) experiences significant packet loss and latency during high bursts of traffic. While interface-level counters do not show RX drops, the internal RX queue statistics indicate drops.ScopeFortiGate VM, GCP.SolutionThe issue is caused by RX queue buffer exhaustion. When the GCP instance presents only one RX queue, the ring buffer descriptors are exhausted during traffic bursts, leading to packet drops. This occurs even if the CPU utilization is not high, as the bottleneck is at the NIC descriptor level rather than the CPU processing level.The following command will list the interface counters. Notice that all the RX drops are zero.diagnose hardware deviceinfo nic port1 Name: port1 Driver: gve Version: 1.3.0 Bus: 0000:00:04.0 HWaddr: 42:01:0a:5c:1a:02 State: up Link: up Mtu: 1460 Supported: Advertised: Speed: 32000half Auto: disabled Rx packets: 14891007 Rx bytes: 1101897774 Rx compressed: 0 Rx dropped: 0 Rx errors: 0 Rx Length err: 0 Use the command below to get more detailed interface stats; it lists the drops on the RX queue.diagnose hardware deviceinfo nic-stats port1 port1 statistics: rx_packets: 1833537831 tx_packets: 1329988458 rx_bytes: 1997339306123 tx_bytes: 1541708454631 -- output trimmed--- rx_queue_drop_cnt[0]: 1716637 rx_no_buffers_posted[0]: 1716637 rx_drops_packet_over_mru[0]: 0 rx_drops_invalid_checksum[0]: 0A non-zero and incrementing values of the counters (rx_queue_drop_cnt and rx_no_buffers_posted) indicate that packets are being dropped at the queue level as the NIC has run out of available descriptors.To resolve the buffer exhaustion, increase the number of RX queues. This provides more descriptors and allows multiple CPUs to process packets in parallel. In Google Cloud Platform, this is achieved by changing the VM instance type to a supported machine series that provides multiple queues.It is possible to notice more queue indexes ([0], [1]) when RX queues are increased.diagnose hardware deviceinfo nic-stats port1 ---output clipped--- Rx dropped: 0 Tx dropped: 0 rx_dropped: 0 tx_dropped: 0 rx_desc_err_dropped_pkt: 0 rx_dropped_pkt[0]: 0 <-- rx_queue_drop_cnt[0]: 0 rx_drops_packet_over_mru[0]: 0 rx_drops_invalid_checksum[0]: 0 rx_dropped_pkt[1]: 0 <-- rx_queue_drop_cnt[1]: 0 rx_drops_packet_over_mru[1]: 0 rx_drops_invalid_checksum[1]: 0

topics.title: How to disable the HTTP TRACE method on FortiClient EMS for Linux
topics.summary: DescriptionSteps to disable the HTTP TRACE method on FortiClient EMS for Linux when vulnerability scanners report that the Apache web server accepts HTTP TRACE requests.ScopeFortiClient EMS.SolutionThe Apache web server used by FortiClient EMS may allow HTTP TRACE requests depending on the underlying Linux distribution and its default Apache configuration.On some RHEL deployments, HTTP TRACE requests may return HTTP 200 OK and echo the original request. On Debian/Ubuntu deployments, Apache may reject these requests by default.To disable the HTTP TRACE method, follow these steps.Verify the HTTP TRACE behavior.From a Windows machine with connectivity to EMS, open PowerShell and execute the following:curl.exe -ki -X TRACE https:// /When TRACE is enabled, the server may return the following:HTTP/1.1 200 OK Server: Apache Content-Type: message/http TRACE / HTTP/1.1 Host: Modify the Apache configuration.Access the underlying Linux operating system with administrative privileges.For RHEL, edit:/etc/httpd/conf/httpd.confFor Debian/Ubuntu, edit the following:/etc/apache2/apache2.confAdd the following directive to the Apache configuration:TraceEnable OffValidate the configuration and restart Apache.For RHEL:sudo httpd -t sudo systemctl restart httpd sudo systemctl status httpdFor Debian/Ubuntu:sudo apache2ctl configtest sudo systemctl restart apache2 sudo systemctl status apache2Ensure the configuration validation completes successfully before restarting the service.Note: Restarting Apache may temporarily interrupt EMS web services. Perform the change during a maintenance window.Verify that HTTP TRACE is disabled.Repeat the TRACE request:curl.exe -ki -X TRACE https:// /The expected response is:HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not AllowedThe server should no longer return HTTP 200 OK with the original TRACE request echoed in the response body.For FortiClient EMS HA deployments, apply the configuration change and verify the results on each EMS application server.

sources.title: IPSec VPN FortiGate to FortiClient
sources.summary: I’m on a FortiGate 61F version 7.4.11 and FortiClient Windows version 7.4.3.I am trying to set up IPSec VPN for my remote users so that I can upgrade the FortiGate (knowing that SSL is no longer supported). I’m running into trouble with Authentication when it comes to PSK vs Peer ID from dialup group. What I want is for the tunnel to accept users from a specific local user group on the FortiGate. My problem is that if I change the Peer Options to Peer ID from dialup group, the Pre-shared Key box goes away. That’s then a problem on FortiClient since I can't leave the PSK box blank. Any help on how to solve this? Thank you! Side Note: I have an IPSec VPN for remote users set up on a different box running 7.6.6 doing exactly what I want. There are more options for Authentication on that version and I can have a PSK and the tell it to use user group I want.

sources.title: FortiGate SD-WAN and Redundant IPsec VPN Requirement
sources.summary: Hi Fortigate Team,The branch currently has a single static ISP connection, while the HO has two independent static ISP connections. Internet traffic at both locations uses their respective local ISPs.We need to configure a redundant IPsec VPN between the branch and HO so that the branch can access internal subnets and servers at the HO through either ISP connection. SD-WAN should be configured at the HO to provide ISP failover and maintain VPN connectivity if the primary ISP fails.SD-WAN should also be configured at the branch. Currently, the branch has only one ISP, but a secondary ISP may be added in the future. The configuration should therefore support ISP failover at the branch when the second ISP becomes available.

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: Logs are not displayed in FortiGate log view when FortiAnalyzer is set as the source
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes the issue where logs are not being displayed in the FortiGate log view when FortiAnalyzer is set as the source.ScopeFortiAnalyzer, FortiGate.SolutionWhen FortiAnalyzer is running in v7.4.11, it does not respond to FortiGate log queries. As a result, logs are not displayed in the FortiGate log view when FortiAnalyzer is set as the source (Whereas if the source is set to memory, logs are displayed).This issue may only affect the FortiGates that are part of the HA cluster.
incidents.symptom: This article describes the issue where logs are not being displayed in the FortiGate log view when FortiAnalyzer is set as the source

incidents.symptom: Instructions to fix ADOM upgrade failure due to a remote certificate invalid error
incidents.solution: An Administrative Domain (ADOM) upgrade from version 7.4 to 7.6 fails due to a remote certificate missing its PEM wrapper, resulting in a certificate invalid error.SymptomsWhen attempting to upgrade an ADOM from version 7.4 to 7.6 in FortiManager, the process fails with the following error message:Fail (errno=-2):This remote certificate is invalidRoot causeThe upgrade fails because one or more remote certificates in the ADOM database are stored without the required PEM wrapper (the -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- and -----END CERTIFICATE----- lines). While the certificate may be valid for current operations, the ADOM upgrade process to version 7.6 rejects certificates that do not follow this standard format. Resolution Restore the PEM wrapper to the affected certificate using a script.Step 1: Identify the problematic certificateSelect Policy & Objects -> Advanced -> Remote Certificate in the root ADOM.Review the entries for certificates that appear incomplete, expired, or use default names.Use the Where Used feature to check if the suspicious certificate is referenced in SAML or PKI user configurations.Run the ADOM Upgrade Readiness check for the root ADOM and export the report to iden

incidents.title: Windows updates fails with enabled Forticlient
incidents.summary: Since last week we experiencing a lot of problems with Windows updates (mostly Windows 11, but there was one Windows 10 among them as well), specifically KB5040442. On about 10% of our Windows clients the update would start and go until 96% and stay there for 10-60 minutes, and then after a restart Windows would tell us that something did go wrong and it would reverse the update. This would require multiple restarts and anything in the order of 2-10h.

sources.title: Windows updates fails with enabled Forticlient
sources.summary: Since last week we experiencing a lot of problems with Windows updates (mostly Windows 11, but there was one Windows 10 among them as well), specifically KB5040442. On about 10% of our Windows clients the update would start and go until 96% and stay there for 10-60 minutes, and then after a restart Windows would tell us that something did go wrong and it would reverse the update. This would require multiple restarts and anything in the order of 2-10h. The usual information sources did not reveal anything unusual with this update round, so it had to be some uncommon conditions here. When Windows was back online, it would sometimes (!) show an error code 0x800f0922, oftenly nothing, and on next restart it would try to install it again (and our employees losing again 4-10h with a working computer). First remedy, as described in the error code was to increase the size of the recovery partition to at least 250MB, but that helped only on one computer. No other things related to the code

sources.title: FortiClient Split Tunnel Not working for Windows Updates
sources.summary: we are using forticlient v7.4.7, today our users brought down their latest updates. Our VPN users are coming back down the VPN tunnel to download their updates, this maxed out our 1GB line. We have Windows updates set in the forticlient to go direct instead of using the tunnel. We also have the .exe and microsoft domain set to got direct. We are still seeing all this traffic coming down the VPN tunnel and then using our web filtering policies on the Fortigate to go out. Can anyone help with this?

aiReview.summary: Erreur -403 lors de l'activation de FortiGate Cloud depuis l'interface graphique sur un cluster HA.
aiReview.symptom: Affichage de l'erreur -403 lors de l'activation de FortiGate Cloud dans l'interface graphique.
aiReview.solution: Vérifier que les deux membres du cluster HA sont enregistrés sous le même compte et remplissent les prérequis d'activation. Sur l'unité primaire, lister les domaines et se connecter avec les commandes 'execute fortiguard-log domain' et 'execute fortiguard-log login'. Si nécessaire, accéder à l'unité secondaire via 'execute ha manage' depuis la primaire et exécuter les mêmes commandes, puis vérifier le statut de l'activation dans l'interface graphique.

incidents.summary: DescriptionA cosmetic issue in FortiOS 7.4.13 causes the FortiLink interface topology view to display "No connected port" for FortiSwitch devices even when MC-LAG is operational.ScopeFortiGate, FortiSwitch.SolutionAfter upgrading a FortiGate HA cluster to FortiOS 7.4.13, the FortiLink interface topology view in the GUI shows "No connected port" for managed FortiSwitch devices. This occurs even if the FortiLink interface and its member links are up: To confirm that the MC-LAG is operational despite the GUI display, run the following commands on the…
incidents.symptom: A cosmetic issue in FortiOS 7.4.13 causes the FortiLink interface topology view to display "No connected port" for FortiSwitch devices even when MC-LAG is operational
incidents.solution: After upgrading a FortiGate HA cluster to FortiOS 7.4.13, the FortiLink interface topology view in the GUI shows "No connected port" for managed FortiSwitch devices. This occurs even if the FortiLink interface and its member links are up: To confirm that the MC-LAG is operational despite the GUI display, run the following commands on the FortiGate:Verify the MC-LAG list and LACP status:diagnose switch-controller switch-info mclag listCheck the Inter-Cluster Link (ICL) status and uptime:diagnose switch-controller switch-info mclag iclVerify the status of the FortiLink interface:get system interface | grep fortilinkCheck port statistics:diagnose switch-controller switch-info port-statsIf the output shows that LACP is active, the ICL is up, and the FortiLink interface status is up, the network traffic is flowing normally and the issue is limited to the GUI display.Root cause:This is a cosmetic GUI issue in FortiOS 7.4.13 build 2933. The data plane remains unaffected, and the MC-LAG adjacency is still formed and operational, but the GUI fails to display the connection status correctly.Permanent solution: This issue is scheduled to be resolved in FortiOS 7.4.14

incidents.title: FortiGate enters Conserve Mode due to WAD memory leak associated with FortiGuard agent
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes an issue where FortiGate enters Conserve Mode due to excessive memory consumption by the WAD process, associated with the FortiGuard agent module 'wad_m_ftgd_agent'.The issue occurs when the WAD process experiences abnormal memory allocation, eventually causing the FortiGate to enter Conserve Mode.ScopeFortiGate, FortiOS 7.6SolutionThe FortiGate may experience excessive memory consumption by the WAD process, eventually entering Conserve Mode.The following symptoms may be observed.Gradually increasing memory…
incidents.symptom: This article describes an issue where FortiGate enters Conserve Mode due to excessive memory consumption by the WAD process, associated with the FortiGuard agent module 'wad_m_ftgd_agent'.The issue occurs when the WAD process experiences abnormal memory allocation, eventually causing the FortiGate to enter Conserve Mode
incidents.solution: The FortiGate may experience excessive memory consumption by the WAD process, eventually entering Conserve Mode.The following symptoms may be observed.Gradually increasing memory consumption by the WAD process.FortiGate periodically entering Conserve Mode.Abnormally high memory allocation associated with 'wad_m_ftgd_agent'.Memory consumption remains high even when traffic levels are relatively stable.Temporary recovery after restarting the affected WAD process.Verify the memory utilizationRun the following commands to check the current memory usage and Conserve Mode status:get system performance status diagnose hardware sysinfo memory diagnose sys print-conserve-infoReview the memory utilization and confirm whether the FortiGate has entered Conserve Mode. The following crash log messages may be observed:service=kernel conserve=on msg="Kernel enters memory conserve mode" service=kernel conserve=exit msg="Kernel exits memory conserve mode"Identify the process consuming excessive memoryRun the following commands:diagnose sys top-mem 20 diagnose sys top-all 1 100 3In the affected environment, one WAD process was consuming approximately 3.15 GB of memory, representing around 40% of the  Contournement : and re solution The recommended solution is to upgrade to a supported FortiOS release containing the correction.The fix was integrated into the following engineering builds.FortiOS 7.6.8 build 3767. This is a special build that can be requested with TAC support.FortiOS 8.0.1As a temporary recovery measure, restarting the affected WAD process may release the accumulated memory. However, this does not resolve the underlying issue, and the memory consumption may increase again.Restarting WAD processes can interrupt active sessions and proxy-based traffic inspection. Perform this action during an appropriate maintenance window.For further information about restarting WAD processes, refer to the related article below.Related articles:Technical Tip: How to restart the WAD processTroubleshooting Tip: Conserve mode due to the IPS engine or WADTechnical Tip: Collect report for WAD high memory related issue for Fortinet TAC assistanceVerify the WAD process while firewall on conserve modeTechnical Tip: Overview of WAD process structure

incidents.title: Copilot is not usable after an upgrade to version 7.6.8 while the Explicit Proxy is in use
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading to version 7.6.8, when using the FortiGate as an Explicit Proxy with the default settings, chat messages for Copilot will be blocked.ScopeFortiOS version 7.6.8+.SolutionAfter upgrading to version 7.6.8, users who are trying to talk to Copilot may see the following message appear:This is similar behaviour to what would occur on versions 7.6.6 and 7.6.7 due to a known issue in those versions tracked under 1308272 and 1257499.
incidents.symptom: After upgrading to version 7.6.8, when using the FortiGate as an Explicit Proxy with the default settings, chat messages for Copilot will be blocked
incidents.solution: After upgrading to version 7.6.8, users who are trying to talk to Copilot may see the following message appear:This is similar behaviour to what would occur on versions 7.6.6 and 7.6.7 due to a known issue in those versions tracked under 1308272 and 1257499. If on these versions, refer to this article instead:Troubleshooting Tip: Resolving Microsoft Copilot access issues with FortiGate inspecting traffic with a policy in proxy-mode and Application Control/IPS.If being on version 7.6.8 and have this issue, check the Forward Traffic logs filtered to the user's source IP. The following log may be visible:The traffic is being allowed by UTM, but denied by the proxy due to 'traffic denied because uri too long'. The maximum length of a request for an Explicit Proxy is defined by 'max-request-length', and this message will be seen when the proxy blocks the request due to exceeding this limit.The following commands can be used to change this limit:config web-proxy profile set max-request-length 64 endOnce this value is changed to the maximum, the traffic is allowed

incidents.title: How to fix error "ssid is used by vap in same vdom" after upgrading version 7.6.8
incidents.summary: DescriptionA commit failure occurs during the FortiManager installation validation stage when an existing wireless Virtual Access Point (VAP) is perceived as a duplicate, preventing the deployment of new SSID configurations.ScopeFortiManagerSolutionDuring the Install Wizard validation stage in FortiManager, the process fails while copying objects. The Install Preview cannot be opened because the validation ends with "Copy Failed".
incidents.symptom: A commit failure occurs during the FortiManager installation validation stage when an existing wireless Virtual Access Point (VAP) is perceived as a duplicate, preventing the deployment of new SSID configurations
incidents.solution: During the Install Wizard validation stage in FortiManager, the process fails while copying objects. The Install Preview cannot be opened because the validation ends with "Copy Failed". The FortiManager log displays the following error:Copy device global objects Copy objects for vdom root Commit failed: error -999 - ssid is used by vap, , in same vdomIf the same duplicate SSID needs to be used in different VAPs, the configuration should be as shown below: Technical Tip: How to use a duplicate SSID (same SSID name, different backend configuration).This particular scenario explains the issue when there is no intetntion to use the same SSID in different VAPs.Checking where the SSID is used with the "Where used" option does not provide extra information about why the conflict occurs.It is possible to unset the failing SSID to the default "fortinet" SSID by running the CLI script against the ADOM and Policy DB:config wireless-controller vap edit " " unset ssid endAfter doing this, the Installation Preview will not throw the same error message and may indicate which VAP the same SSID will be installed on. If it is not the correct configuration, it is possible to run the same script again

incidents.title: Analytics retention status remains one day below the configured limit and does not reach 100% in FortiAnalyzer 7.6.6.
incidents.summary: DescriptionOn FortiAnalyzer 7.6.6, the analytics retention status shows 89 out of 90 configured days (98%) and never reaches the full 90 days (100%).Scope FortiAnalyzer.SolutionThis is a known issue in FortiAnalyzer 7.6.6 where the analytics retention does not correctly reach the configured limit.Solution:Upgrade FortiAnalyzer. Upgrade the device to one of the following versions where this issue is resolved:FortiAnalyzer 7.6.7, build 3685 and laterFortiAnalyzer 8.0.0, build 0054 and laterWorkaround: If an upgrade is not immediately possible, increase…
incidents.symptom: On FortiAnalyzer 7.6.6, the analytics retention status shows 89 out of 90 configured days (98%) and never reaches the full 90 days (100%)
incidents.solution: This is a known issue in FortiAnalyzer 7.6.6 where the analytics retention does not correctly reach the configured limit.Solution:Upgrade FortiAnalyzer. Upgrade the device to one of the following versions where this issue is resolved:FortiAnalyzer 7.6.7, build 3685 and laterFortiAnalyzer 8.0.0, build 0054 and later Contournement : If an upgrade is not immediately possible, increase the configured retention period by one day. For example, if 90 days of retention are required, set the "Keep logs for Analytics" setting to 91 days. The system trimming process will remove the boundary day, effectively leaving the required 90 days of data. Apply this same logic to any other ADOM configured with a different retention period by adding one day to the current setting

incidents.summary: DescriptionThe pre-login disclaimer is not displayed as configured when accessing the FortiGate GUI, even though the pre-login disclaimer has been configured.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionThe FortiGate is configured with separate MGMT and Traffic VDOMs. Users access the GUI through a web browser using the Management IP address assigned to an interface in the MGMT VDOM. The pre_admin-disclaimer-text message is configured under the following path in the Global VDOM. config system replacemsg admin "pre_admin-disclaimer-text" set buffer "PRE WARNING: This is a…
incidents.symptom: The pre-login disclaimer is not displayed as configured when accessing the FortiGate GUI, even though the pre-login disclaimer has been configured
incidents.solution: The FortiGate is configured with separate MGMT and Traffic VDOMs. Users access the GUI through a web browser using the Management IP address assigned to an interface in the MGMT VDOM. The pre_admin-disclaimer-text message is configured under the following path in the Global VDOM. config system replacemsg admin "pre_admin-disclaimer-text" set buffer "PRE WARNING: This is a private computer system. Unauthorized access or use is prohibited and subject to prosecution and/or disciplinary action. Any use of this system constitutes consent to monitoring at all times and users are not entitled to any expectation of privacy. If monitoring reveals possible evidence of violation of criminal statutes, this evidence and any other related information, including identification information about the user, may be provided to law enforcement officials. If monitoring reveals violations of security regulations or unauthorized use, employees who violate security regulations or make unauthorized use of this system are subject to appropriate disciplinary action. end However, when users access the GUI, a different disclaimer message is displayed instead of the configured pre_admin-disclaimer-text. To trou Contournement : Delete the replacemsg-group configured in the MGMT VDOM.config vdom edit config system replacemsg-group delete default next end

incidents.title: FortiAP clients unable to obtain IP address via DHCP
incidents.summary: DescriptionWireless clients cannot receive an IP address from the DHCP server despite the server sending DHCP Offer packets. This is caused by insufficient Power over Ethernet (PoE) amperage provided to the FortiAP.ScopeFortiAP, FortiGate, FortiSwitch.SolutionSymptoms: Wireless clients can see the SSID and enter the correct password, but they fail to obtain an IP address via DHCP. Packet captures show that the DHCP server responds to the DHCP Discovery with a DHCP Offer, but the client never sends a DHCP Request.Root cause: The FortiAP is connected…
incidents.symptom: Wireless clients cannot receive an IP address from the DHCP server despite the server sending DHCP Offer packets. This is caused by insufficient Power over Ethernet (PoE) amperage provided to the FortiAP
incidents.solution: Symptoms: Wireless clients can see the SSID and enter the correct password, but they fail to obtain an IP address via DHCP. Packet captures show that the DHCP server responds to the DHCP Discovery with a DHCP Offer, but the client never sends a DHCP Request.Root cause: The FortiAP is connected to a PoE source that provides insufficient amperage. In this case, the PoE source provided 55V - 0.6A, while the FortiAP requires 55V - 1.09A to operate correctly. This power deficiency prevents the FortiAP from processing the DHCP handshake properly.Resolution:Verify the power requirements of the FortiAP model in use.Check the PoE output specifications of the switch or PoE injector providing power to the FortiAP.Ensure the PoE source meets or exceeds the required voltage and amperage (e.g., 55V - 1.09A).Connect the FortiAP to a PoE switch or injector that provides the required power specifications.Verify that wireless clients can now successfully obtain an IP address via DHCP.Troubleshooting steps to identify the issue:If clients cannot obtain an IP address, perform the following captures to determine where the DHCP process fails:Run a sniffer on the FortiAP CLI to monitor DHCP traffic:diag_

incidents.title: False positive anti-replay (replayed packet) drops on NP7 platforms when npu-offload is enabled on phase1-interface
incidents.summary: DescriptionAnti-replay (replayed packet) drops are seen on NP7 platforms at or around rekeys when npu-offload is enabled on phase1-interface.ScopeFortiOS, NP7 platforms.SolutionOn NP7-based FortiGates such as FortiGate-401F, inbound ESP packets consisting of three or more fragments can cause anti-replay errors, even though the packets are neither duplicated or replayed.WorkaroundImplement one of the following configurations to prevent the unintended drops from anti-replayDisable npu-offload on phase1-interface of the affected tunnel.config vpn ipsec…
incidents.symptom: Anti-replay (replayed packet) drops are seen on NP7 platforms at or around rekeys when npu-offload is enabled on phase1-interface
incidents.solution: On NP7-based FortiGates such as FortiGate-401F, inbound ESP packets consisting of three or more fragments can cause anti-replay errors, even though the packets are neither duplicated or replayed Contournement : Implement one of the following configurations to prevent the unintended drops from anti-replayDisable npu-offload on phase1-interface of the affected tunnel.config vpn ipsec phase1-interface edit set npu-offload disable next end Disable anti-replay on the phase2-interface of the affected tunnel. This disables all anti-replay drops.config vpn ipsec phase2-interface edit set replay disable next end Enable NP7 ip-reassembly (this is not recommended in most environments that would be affected by this issue, since it causes additional latency in environments with many packets consisting of three or more fragments.)config system npu config ip-reassembly set status enable end end Resolution An enhancement is scheduled for FortiOS 8.0.3 to enable configuring the espff-proc option under config system npu. This setting affects how the NP7 counts fragmented ESP packets when ip-reassembly is disabled.config system npu set espff-proc endWhen to disable espff-proc:Continuous inbound ESP traffic fragmented into more than two fragments.Consistent anti-replay (replayed packet) drops observed, especially during or immediately after a rekey.Disabling npu-offload on the phase1-interface no longer show

incidents.summary: DescriptionSteps to repair FortiDeceptor IP ban functionality with multiple VDOMs on a FortiGate operating in a multi-VDOM environment. incidents.symptom: Steps to repair FortiDeceptor IP ban functionality with multiple VDOMs on a FortiGate operating in a multi-VDOM environment. Note that FortiDeceptor automatic quarantine actions apply only to the root or management VDOM on FortiGate devices, so they do not block traffic in other VDOMs
incidents.solution: When integrating FortiDeceptor with FortiGate for automatic quarantine, the IP ban action only appears in the root or management VDOM. The quarantine does not propagate to other VDOMs or devices in the Security Fabric, and traffic in those VDOMs is not blocked.The FortiDeceptor integration uses a REST API to send Fabric events to FortiGate. aiReview.summary: Dysfonctionnement de l'intégration de quarantaine FortiDeceptor dans les VDOMs non-management sur FortiGate.
aiReview.symptom: Les actions de quarantaine automatique de FortiDeceptor s'appliquent uniquement au VDOM root ou management sur les appareils FortiGate, ce qui fait qu'elles ne bloquent pas le trafic dans les autres VDOMs.
aiReview.impact: La quarantaine ne se propage pas aux autres VDOMs ou appareils de la Security Fabric, et le trafic dans ces VDOMs n'est pas bloqué.
aiReview.solution: Acheminer le trafic via un "npu.vlink" vers le VDOM root pour bloquer le trafic, ou accorder au connecteur du Security Fabric l'accès aux VDOMs non-management via les commandes CLI appropriées.
aiReview.note: La source est incomplète sur la fin de la commande CLI.

incidents.title: FortiSwitch SCP Not Working After Upgrade – Error 501: Permission Denied
incidents.summary: DescriptionAfter upgrading the FortiSwitch, SCP file transfers stopped working and returned the following error:501 - Permission DeniedScopeFortiSwitch 7.6.7 and later releases.SolutionConfiguration and FindingsThe following TACACS+ remote authentication configuration was observed on the FortiSwitch:edit "name" set remote-auth enable set trusthost1 x.x.x.x x.x.x.x set trusthost2 x.x.x.x x.x.x.x set accprofile "no_access" set wildcard enable set remote-group "group" set accprofile-override enable nextThe following observations were made during…
incidents.symptom: After upgrading the FortiSwitch, SCP file transfers stopped working and returned the following error:501 - Permission Denied
incidents.solution: Configuration and FindingsThe following TACACS+ remote authentication configuration was observed on the FortiSwitch:edit "name" set remote-auth enable set trusthost1 x.x.x.x x.x.x.x set trusthost2 x.x.x.x x.x.x.x set accprofile "no_access" set wildcard enable set remote-group "group" set accprofile-override enable nextThe following observations were made during troubleshooting:The accprofile-override setting is enabled.During authentication, the TACACS+ server returns the super_admin access profile.Direct SSH access using the same TACACS+ account works successfully, and the expected administrative privileges are available. Solution Starting from FortiSwitch 7.6.7, SCP is no longer supported.To back up the switch configuration, use one of the supported file transfer protocols: SFTP, FTP, or TFTP.Unlike the previous SCP-based approach, starting from FortiSwitch 7.6.7, configuration backups must be initiated directly from the FortiSwitch. In this process, the FortiSwitch establishes an outbound connection to the SFTP, FTP, or TFTP server to transfer the configuration backup.Note: Use SFTP, FTP, or TFTP as alternatives to SCP when backing up FortiSwitch configurations on version 7.6.7

incidents.title: Primary FortiGate GUI unavailable with "SSL_ERROR_BAD_MAC_READ" error after upgrading to 7.4.13
incidents.summary: DescriptionThe web management GUI of the primary FortiGate unit becomes inaccessible with a TLS MAC error when virtual patching is enabled on a local-in policy.ScopeFortiGate, FortiManager.SolutionSymptomsAfter upgrading a FortiGate High Availability cluster to FortiGate version 7.4.13, the HTTPS management GUI of the primary unit is unavailable. Users attempting to connect via browser receive the following error message:Secure Connection Failed The page you are trying to view cannot be shown because the authenticity of the received data could not be…
incidents.symptom: The web management GUI of the primary FortiGate unit becomes inaccessible with a TLS MAC error when virtual patching is enabled on a local-in policy
incidents.solution: SymptomsAfter upgrading a FortiGate High Availability cluster to FortiGate version 7.4.13, the HTTPS management GUI of the primary unit is unavailable. Users attempting to connect via browser receive the following error message:Secure Connection Failed The page you are trying to view cannot be shown because the authenticity of the received data could not be verified. Error Code: SSL_ERROR_BAD_MAC_READThe following conditions are observed:SSH access to the primary unit remains functional.The management GUI of the secondary unit remains accessible.The issue is reproducible by enabling virtual patching on the local-in policy covering management HTTPS traffic. Root causeA regression in FortiOS 7.4.13 causes a TLS record MAC failure during the handshake when virtual-patch is enabled on a local-in policy that processes management HTTPS traffic on the primary unit of a High-Availability cluster. Re solution The fix for this issue is scheduled for release in FortiOS 8.0.3.Use one of the following workarounds to restore GUI access Contournement : 1: Disable virtual patchingDisable the virtual-patch setting on the local-in policy that matches management HTTPS traffic.Connect to the FortiGate via SSH.Run the following commands:config firewall local-in-policy edit set virtual-patch disable next end Workaround 2: Use a non-self-signed certificateChange the administrative server certificate from a self-signed certificate to a CA-signed certificate.Connect to the FortiGate via SSH.Run the following commands:config system global set admin-server-cert Fortinet_GUI_Server end

incidents.summary: DescriptionTraffic sourced from a FortiGate VLAN interface fails to communicate over a VXLAN tunnel when the LAN1 interface is part of the same software switch due to a MAC address conflict.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptoms.A user configures a VXLAN tunnel between two FortiGate devices. The VXLAN interface and the LAN1 interface are members of the same software switch. In this configuration, the following behavior occurs:Host-to-host traffic across the VXLAN tunnel works normally.Traffic sourced from the FortiGate VLAN interface fails to reach the…
incidents.symptom: Traffic sourced from a FortiGate VLAN interface fails to communicate over a VXLAN tunnel when the LAN1 interface is part of the same software switch due to a MAC address conflict
incidents.solution: Symptoms.A user configures a VXLAN tunnel between two FortiGate devices. The VXLAN interface and the LAN1 interface are members of the same software switch. In this configuration, the following behavior occurs:Host-to-host traffic across the VXLAN tunnel works normally.Traffic sourced from the FortiGate VLAN interface fails to reach the remote site.Communication works if the LAN1 interface is removed from the software switch or if a different interface (such as LAN2) is used instead. Root cause.The issue is caused by a MAC address conflict. On certain FortiGate models, the Current_HWaddr (Virtual MAC) for the LAN1 interface is derived from the HA group-id. If two separate FortiGate clusters use the same group-id, they assign the identical Virtual MAC address to their respective LAN1 interfaces.When a VLAN interface is created on top of a software switch, it inherits the MAC address of the first member interface. If LAN1 is the first member, the VLAN interface uses the duplicated Virtual MAC. incidents.symptom: Upgrading a FortiGate device to version 7.6.8 may cause the web administration interface to become unavailable, resulting in the firewall sending TCP resets to HTTPS requests
incidents.solution: Root causeIf the FortiGate belongs to the security fabric, the root is running 7.4.x, and the leaf FortiGate version is 7.6.8: the stability of the web administration service will be affected and application crash autod will be generated. Resolution Upgrade the FortiGate root to the same version of the leaf FortiGate, or apply the following workaround:config automation setting set fabric-sync disable endTroubleshooting the web interfaceIf the web interface does not respond, verify the current management port settings using the following command:get system global | grep -E "admin-sport|management-port"Run the https and http_auth daemons commands. If no information is shown, review whether the TCP port for the admin port is open, and whether the gnum 10000e and 10000f policies show the https is open to the interface the packet is entering through

incidents.symptom: The connectivity failure observed when accessing the LDAP server behind FortiGate from FortiAuthenticator ('FAC') Cloud via a Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) tunnel
incidents.solution: To configure the ZTNA access to the LDAP server from FortiAuthenticator, refer to this document: Accessing an AD server with a zero trust tunnel on FortiAuthenticator.The following errors are observed on FortiAuthenticator when trying to query for group information.Sample error 1:As observed in the packet capture taken on the FortiGate (FGT), the TLS handshake fails with a "Certificate Unknown" alert sent from the FortiAuthenticator (FAC) end.Sample error 2:For the ZTNA server certificate, the self-signed certificate generated on the FortiGate (FGT) was used. The corresponding Sub-CA and CA certificates were uploaded to FortiAuthenticator (FAC) to establish the certificate trust chain. However, despite importing these certificates, the same TLS handshake failure with a "Certificate Unknown" alert from the FAC end continues to occur.Resolution:It is recommended to use either a public CA-signed certificate or a FortiAuthenticator (FAC) local CA-signed certificate as the ZTNA server certificate on the FortiGate (FGT), instead of using the self-signed certificate generated by the FGT. This ensures proper certificate chain validation and avoids TLS handshake failures due to certificate

incidents.title: ZTNA destination access is slow when IPv6 is enabled on the Windows network adapter
incidents.summary: DescriptionConnections to ZTNA destinations over RDP or HTTP take 10 to 20 seconds when IPv6 is enabled on the network adapter of a Windows endpoint running FortiClient. This article describes the symptoms, the cause, and the workarounds.ScopeFortiClient 7.4.7 and 7.4.9 for Windows with ZTNA enabled, managed by FortiClient EMS, connecting to FQDN-based destinations through a FortiGate ZTNA access proxy.SolutionSymptomsConnection delay: connecting to a ZTNA destination over RDP or HTTP takes 10 to 20 seconds.DNS behavior: nslookup for the ZTNA…
incidents.symptom: Connections to ZTNA destinations over RDP or HTTP take 10 to 20 seconds when IPv6 is enabled on the network adapter of a Windows endpoint running FortiClient. This article describes the symptoms, the cause, and the workarounds
incidents.solution: SymptomsConnection delay: connecting to a ZTNA destination over RDP or HTTP takes 10 to 20 seconds.DNS behavior: nslookup for the ZTNA destination FQDN times out or returns a non-existent domain response.IPv6 dependency: disabling IPv6 on the network adapter of the endpoint reduces the connection time to approximately 1 second.Unaffected destinations: destinations configured with literal IP addresses do not trigger a DNS lookup and are not affected.CauseFortiClient intercepts ZTNA traffic for FQDN-based destinations through a DNS proxy. An IPv6 DNS server bypasses this proxy, so FortiClient blocks IPv6 DNS queries by design while ZTNA is active. ZTNA does not currently support IPv6 DNS resolution.The Windows DNS client sends the query over IPv6 first, waits for a retry timeout of approximately 10 seconds, and then falls back to IPv4. This wait produces the delay.The FortiClient diagnostic logs confirm the condition with entries similar to the following.Block IPV6 DNS query: remoteIp=2001:db8::53 remotePort=53The limitation applies to DNS resolution over IPv6. incidents.symptom: DHCP IP address assignment failure only on specific VLANs 97 and 98 on a Bridge mode SSID on the FortiAP-221E model
incidents.solution: VLAN 97 and 98 are reserved for Internet use on the FortiAP-W2 models. Therefore, do not use those VLAN IDs in the FortiAP management VLAN, SSID static VLAN, and dynamically assigned VLAN. Refer to Reserved VLAN IDs.Since the FortiAP-221E is now a legacy model, and this behavior is as per the design and is expected on the E series FortiAP models, there are currently no plans to modify this functionality on this model. To move forward, consider either:Using alternative VLAN IDs instead of 97 and 98, or:Upgrading to a newer FortiAP model, as the current F, G, and K series FortiAPs support these VLAN IDs

incidents.symptom: When the session count on the FortiGate is not high, but softirq is high and contributes to HA port flapping:The HA port flapping causes HA role flap, and results in MAC address flapping on the upstream and downstream switch that connects to it.This issue occurred on an HA cluster that has session synchronization across the members.Note:There could be other factors that could cause high usage of softIRQ on the FortiGate, and initial troubleshooting should be done to determine what could have caused the high softIRQ:Technical Tip: Understanding and analyzing high SoftIRQCommon factors that cause high softirq:Layer 2 loopingBroadcast stormDoS/DDoS attackHigh volumes of denied traffic or asymmetric routingExcessive traffic volume and high session setup rates

incidents.title: Intermittent SSL/TLS failures on website portals with Deep SSL Inspection and IPS (flow-based) — blank page / ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR
incidents.summary: DescriptionWhen a firewall policy runs flow-based inspection with Deep SSL Inspection and an IPS sensor, an HTTPS application can intermittently fail mid-session.Scope FortiOS 7.6.7.SolutionSymptomsUsers may experience intermittent failures when loading or submitting content on specific websites, resulting in a blank page.The browser may report net::ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR, with the failed request showing:Status = 0No HTTP versionNo server IP addressNo response bytes receivedFortiGate SSL inspection logs indicate that the affected sessions are…
incidents.symptom: When a firewall policy runs flow-based inspection with Deep SSL Inspection and an IPS sensor, an HTTPS application can intermittently fail mid-session
incidents.solution: SymptomsUsers may experience intermittent failures when loading or submitting content on specific websites, resulting in a blank page.The browser may report net::ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR, with the failed request showing:Status = 0No HTTP versionNo server IP addressNo response bytes receivedFortiGate SSL inspection logs indicate that the affected sessions are otherwise processed successfully, including:action="accept" and utmaction="allow"Successful SSL/TLS handshake completion (handshake-done)mitm="yes" indicating successful deep inspectionA valid server certificateIn some cases, traffic flows terminate with action="client-rst" while utmaction="allow" remains unchanged.IPS debugging shows that the corresponding session is finalized (ips_tcp_layer_fini) during an idle period. When the client subsequently attempts to close or reuse the same connection, the IPS engine can no longer locate the associated session. As a result:The IPS engine reports that the session cannot be found.The subsequent request may be decoded incorrectly, often appearing as a smaller or incomplete request.The client may establish a new connection using a different source port.IPS Debug CollectionEnable IPS debugg Contournement : The following workarounds have been successfully implemented in affected environments:Option 1: Downgrade to an Earlier IPS Engine BuildUse an IPS engine version before 7.6.1183. IPS Engine 7.6.1182 has been verified not to exhibit this behavior.If FortiGuard automatic updates are enabled:Temporarily disable scheduled IPS engine updates after reverting to 7.6.1182.Prevent the device from automatically upgrading back to a later affected build.Re-enable automatic updates once a fixed IPS engine version is deployed.Option 2: Exempt the Affected Destination from Deep InspectionAdd the affected FQDN to the SSL/SSH Inspection Profile Exempt List to bypass deep inspection for the destination. Resolution Upgrade to an IPS engine version that contains the fix.The issue has been resolved in:IPS engine 7.6.9 (Build 1202) on the 7.6 branch IPS engine 8.0.3 (Build 0053) on the 8.0 branchAfter upgrading to a fixed IPS engine build, FortiGuard automatic updates can be safely re-enabled

When the client subsequently attempts to close or reuse the same connection, the IPS engine can no longer locate the associated session. As a result:The IPS engine reports that the session cannot be found.The subsequent request may be decoded incorrectly, often appearing as a smaller or incomplete request.The client may establish a new connection using a different source port.IPS Debug CollectionEnable IPS debugg Contournement : The following workarounds have been successfully implemented in affected environments:Option 1: Downgrade to an Earlier IPS Engine BuildUse an IPS engine version before 7.6.1183. IPS Engine 7.6.1182 has been verified not to exhibit this behavior.If FortiGuard automatic updates are enabled:Temporarily disable scheduled IPS engine updates after reverting to 7.6.1182.Prevent the device from automatically upgrading back to a later affected build.Re-enable automatic updates once a fixed IPS engine version is deployed.Option 2: Exempt the Affected Destination from Deep InspectionAdd the affected FQDN to the SSL/SSH Inspection Profile Exempt List to bypass deep inspection for the destination. Resolution Upgrade to an IPS engine version that contains the fix.The issue has been resolved in:IPS engine 7.6.9 (Build 1202) on the 7.6 branch IPS engine 8.0.3 (Build 0053) on the 8.0 branchAfter upgrading to a fixed IPS engine build, FortiGuard automatic updates can be safely re-enabled

incidents.summary: DescriptionCertain fields are missing from Antivirus logs (Message ID 8195) when the HTTP Content-Type is multipart/form-data and proxy-based inspection is used.ScopeFortiGate.SolutionSymptoms.When using proxy-based inspection for HTTP or HTTPS traffic with a multipart/form-dataContent-Type, the Antivirus logs (Message ID 8195 for monitored actions and Message ID 8194 for blocked actions) do not contain the following fields:agent.httpmethod.referralurl.This issue only affects the log information and does not impact the actual Antivirus detection,…
incidents.symptom: Certain fields are missing from Antivirus logs (Message ID 8195) when the HTTP Content-Type is multipart/form-data and proxy-based inspection is used
incidents.solution: Symptoms.When using proxy-based inspection for HTTP or HTTPS traffic with a multipart/form-dataContent-Type, the Antivirus logs (Message ID 8195 for monitored actions and Message ID 8194 for blocked actions) do not contain the following fields:agent.httpmethod.referralurl.This issue only affects the log information and does not impact the actual Antivirus detection, monitoring, blocking, or traffic flow.Root cause.Bug ID 1281140 (Resolved issues) in FortiOS causes these specific fields to be omitted from the log output when the traffic is processed using proxy-based inspection and contains multipart form data.Resolution.Affected versions:FortiOS version 7.6.6.FortiOS version 8.0.0.Resolved versions:FortiOS version 7.6.7.FortiOS version 8.0.1.Resolved issues 8.0.1Resolved issues 7.6.7Upgrade the FortiGate to FortiOS version 7.6.7 or FortiOS version 8.0.1 Contournement : If an upgrade is not immediately possible, change the firewall policy inspection mode from proxy-based to flow-based. This issue does not occur in flow-based inspection mode.CLI configuration:config firewall policy edit set inspection-mode flow next endImportant:Before changing the inspection mode, review the security profiles applied to the firewall policy and verify their compatibility with flow-based inspection

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: SSH Deep Scan setting is disabled automatically after saving the SSL/SSH inspection profile
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a known issue where SSH Deep Scan cannot be successfully configured in the SSL/SSH inspection profile.ScopeFortiGate low-end models.SolutionOn certain entry-level FortiGate models (such as 40F, 50G, 60F, and 60E) with 2 GB of memory, after upgrading FortiOS from versions 7.4.8 to 7.4.10 or 7.4.11, an unexpected behavior is observed where the SSH Deep Scan option under the SSL/SSH inspection profile is no longer retained or cannot be enabled.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a known issue where SSH Deep Scan cannot be successfully configured in the SSL/SSH inspection profile
incidents.solution: On certain entry-level FortiGate models (such as 40F, 50G, 60F, and 60E) with 2 GB of memory, after upgrading FortiOS from versions 7.4.8 to 7.4.10 or 7.4.11, an unexpected behavior is observed where the SSH Deep Scan option under the SSL/SSH inspection profile is no longer retained or cannot be enabled. When attempting to enable it, the feature appears enabled; however, after returning to the same screen, the feature remains disabled. Additionally, the related CLI commands are no longer available, even though the option is still displayed in the GUI. When attempting to enable the feature through the CLI, the command cannot be found, as shown below.FGR60F-2 # config firewall ssl-ssh-profile FGR60F-2 (ssl-ssh-profile) # edit dip-certificate-inspection new entry 'dip-certificate-inspection' added FGR60F-2 (dip-certificate-inspection) # config ssh command parse error before 'ssh' Command fail. Return code 1 FGR60F-2 (dip-certificate-inspection) # endThis is a known issue affecting certain entry-level FortiGate models running specific FortiOS versions. The issue is scheduled to be resolved in FortiOS v7.4.13, v7.6.7, and v8.0.0

incidents.title: FortiGate EMS fabric connector fails to validate CA certificate
incidents.summary: DescriptionThe FortiClient/EMS fabric connector on FortiGate version 7.4.12 rejects a valid publicly signed FortiClient/EMS web server certificate with a CA not recognized error. This article describes the incident details, debugging, and solution of the issue.ScopeFortiGate, FortiClient EMS.SolutionAfter upgrading FortiOS, the FortiGate EMS fabric connector may fail to validate a valid EMS server certificate and display the error EMS server certificate is not signed by any known CA.
incidents.symptom: The FortiClient/EMS fabric connector on FortiGate version 7.4.12 rejects a valid publicly signed FortiClient/EMS web server certificate with a CA not recognized error. This article describes the incident details, debugging, and solution of the issue
incidents.solution: After upgrading FortiOS, the FortiGate EMS fabric connector may fail to validate a valid EMS server certificate and display the error EMS server certificate is not signed by any known CA. The issue may occur even when the certificate chain is valid, and the required CA certificates are installed on the FortiGate. Also, it might be resolved after revalidating or reinstalling the certificate chain in the FortiGate certificate store. Enable the following debug commands, reproduce the issue by testing the EMS connection, and then disable debugging.diagnose debug reset diagnose debug application fcnacd -1 diagnose debug console timestamp enable diagnose endpoint filter show-large-data yes diagnose debug enableAfter reproducing the issue, stop debugging:diagnose debug disable diagnose debug resetThe message "Could not verify EMS cert chain" indicates that certificate-chain validation failed. The message "EMS server certificate is not signed by any known CA" points to a CA trust or certificate-validation failure, but does not by itself prove that the CA certificate is missing. Check the configured CA reference and whether the certificate chain is being validated correctly.The message "EMS Contournement : Review the EMS connector configuration under "config endpoint-control fctems". If stale certificate verification settings are suspected, unset the certificate fingerprint and verified common name, then re-verify the EMS connection.config endpoint-control fctems edit 1 unset certificate-fingerprint unset verified-cn end endRelated Article:Troubleshooting Tip: Unable to connect FortiClient EMS due to a server certificate

incidents.title: Troubleshooting Tip: FortiClient installer showing '{"result": {"retval": -1, "message": "File not found"}}' in email invitation
incidents.summary: DescriptionThis article describes a FortiClient installer showing '{"result": {"retval": -1, "message": "File not found"}}' in the email invitation.ScopeFortiClient EMS version 7.4.8 and FortiClient EMS Cloud.SolutionWhen a user selects the FortiClient installer download link in an EMS invitation email, the browser displays the following error:The installer filename in the invitation URL may contain uppercase characters, while the actual filename on the EMS server uses lowercase characters.
incidents.symptom: This article describes a FortiClient installer showing '{"result": {"retval": -1, "message": "File not found"}}' in the email invitation
incidents.solution: When a user selects the FortiClient installer download link in an EMS invitation email, the browser displays the following error:The installer filename in the invitation URL may contain uppercase characters, while the actual filename on the EMS server uses lowercase characters. Since filenames can be case-sensitive depending on the underlying file system, this mismatch may cause the download to fail Contournement : Change the installer filename in the URL to lowercase.For example, change:https://10.47.4.59:10443/installers/default/7.4.8/FortiClientSetup_7.4.8_x64.exeTo:https://10.47.4.59:10443/installers/default/7.4.8/forticlientsetup_7.4.8_x64.exeNote: This is a workaround for the known issue documented in the FortiClient EMS 7.4.8 release notes. Refer to the applicable release notes for further information.Release notes: New known issues.Planned improvement:An improvement related to installer download is currently planned for FortiClient EMS 7.4.9. incidents.title: Upgrading FortiGate devices to latest patch release without a firmware license
incidents.summary: DescriptionInstructions for initiating a patch-level upgrade when the device has no support contract.ScopeFortiOS 7.4 and 7.6FortiGate devices with no firmware contract.SolutionIn FortiOS 7.4.2 and higher, it is not possible to upgrade to later firmware versions in the GUI if the device has an expired firmware license.The FortiOS GUI will display the warnings such as "This is a FortiOS v7.4.5-build2702 firmware image that cannot be installed because the device's FortiGuard license for firmware upgrades could not be verified or may have expired.
incidents.symptom: Instructions for initiating a patch-level upgrade when the device has no support contract
incidents.solution: In FortiOS 7.4.2 and higher, it is not possible to upgrade to later firmware versions in the GUI if the device has an expired firmware license.The FortiOS GUI will display the warnings such as "This is a FortiOS v7.4.5-build2702 firmware image that cannot be installed because the device's FortiGuard license for firmware upgrades could not be verified or may have expired. Verify or renew the license to install upgrades." Even if a device has no valid support contract, it is strongly recommended to maintain a patched firmware version. See available upgrade methods below. Upgrade using forced FortiGuard update:This method applies to the following FortiOS firmware versions:FortiOS 7.4.8 and higherFortiOS 7.6.4 and higherThese firmware versions support forced firmware upgrade within the same minor firmware version even if the device does not have an existing firmware license.Verify the FortiGate has DNS and internet access, and use execute auto-upgrade check-for-new-image: FortiGate-40F # execute auto-upgrade check-for-new-image Manually triggering auto-upgrade new image check... Auto-upgrade new image check triggered. FortiGate-40F # Firmware Update from Management Service Upgrade to i

incidents.title: FortiManager version 7.6.8 trying to install ssl-ssh-profile settings that are not supported on 2GB FortiGate devices
incidents.summary: DescriptionTroubleshooting steps for installation failure in FortiManager version 7.6.8 due to the 'udp-not-quic' option under 'config firewall ssl-ssh-profile' when installing to FortiGate models with 2GB of memory.ScopeFortiManager. SolutionIn version 7.6.8, FortiManager has added some lines to the configuration to push. For example:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit "custom-deep-inspection" config https set udp-not-quick allow end config dot set udp-not-quick allow end next endWhen installing on FortiGate models with 2GB of memory, this change…
incidents.symptom: Troubleshooting steps for installation failure in FortiManager version 7.6.8 due to the 'udp-not-quic' option under 'config firewall ssl-ssh-profile' when installing to FortiGate models with 2GB of memory
incidents.solution: In version 7.6.8, FortiManager has added some lines to the configuration to push. For example:config firewall ssl-ssh-profile edit "custom-deep-inspection" config https set udp-not-quick allow end config dot set udp-not-quick allow end next endWhen installing on FortiGate models with 2GB of memory, this change causes the installation to fail.These models do not support this option in FortiOS version 7.6.This behavior is due to a known issue, with ID 1352524 Contournement : Set 'udp-not-quic' to 'block' in the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Set udp-not-quic to block in the https and dot sections of the affected SSL/SSH profiles.Go to Policy & Objects -> Advanced.Select the CLI Configurations tab.In the left pane, under firewall, select ssl-ssh-profile.Select the affected profile (for example, custom-deep-inspection), then select Edit.In the Edit firewall ssl-ssh-profile window, scroll to the https section and set udp-not-quic to block.Scroll to the dot section and set udp-not-quic to block.Select OK.Repeat steps 4 to 7 for each SSL/SSH profile that is used by the 2GB FortiGate devices.Install the policy package again.Note: Some models may not accept this setting. For example, a comment on this article reports 'Operation not supported. detail: object not support' on a FortiGate 50G. Contact Fortinet Support if the error persists.Fix: A fix is expected in FortiManager firmware versions 7.6.9 and 8.0.3.Related document:Known issues
